He was celebrated for his masterful tailoring, innovative techniques, and the dramatic, narrative-driven fashion shows that became his signature. McQueen's work often explored themes of nature, history, and the macabre, earning him a reputation as a visionary in the fashion industry.
alexander-mcqueen.o: The style uses highly realistic, softly lit fashion portraiture focused on elaborate white lace, beadwork, pearls, crystals, and reflective silver ornament. Restrained ivory and silver tones, selective focus, candlelit backgrounds, and tight editorial framing create a ceremonial, museum-like atmosphere across the portraits.

alexander-millar.a: Alexander Millar is a contemporary Scottish artist known for his evocative depictions of working-class life and urban landscapes. His work often captures the essence of industrial towns, focusing on the everyday lives of ordinary people, imbued with a sense of nostalgia and emotion.
alexander-millar.o: Across all four images, solitary urban figures are rendered with visible, broad, textured brushwork and strongly blocked silhouettes. Cool blue dusk, deep shadows, selective red accents, industrial structures, and glowing streetlamps create a moody, cinematic atmosphere with expressive painterly surfaces.

alexander-payne.a: Alexander Payne is an American filmmaker known for his work in the film industry, particularly in the genre of comedy-drama. He has received critical acclaim for his ability to blend humor with poignant storytelling, often focusing on human relationships and personal journeys. Some of his notable films include 'Sideways,' 'The Descendants,' and 'Nebraska,' which have earned him several awards and nominations.
alexander-payne.o: The style combines cinematic portrait framing with a graphic, illustrative treatment: strong contour lines, simplified painted shapes, selective texture, and carefully observed facial features. Across the photographic and drawn-looking scenes, it favors moody warm shadows, high contrast, thoughtful figures, and urban architectural settings with a restrained retro-editorial atmosphere.

alexander-rodchenko.a: Alexander Rodchenko was a Russian artist, sculptor, photographer, and graphic designer, known for his pioneering work in the Constructivist movement. His innovative approach to art and design emphasized geometric abstraction and the use of modern materials and techniques. Rodchenko's work often explored themes of industrialization and urbanization, reflecting the dynamic changes in Soviet society during the early 20th century.
alexander-rodchenko.o: The style combines stark monochrome portrait fragments with angular, layered collage shapes and dramatic cropping. Heavy contrast, visible grain, rough linework, and overlapping photographic and graphic elements create an expressive, surreal editorial image language.

alexandr-averin.a: Alexandr Averin is a Russian painter known for his impressionistic style, focusing on serene and romantic scenes often depicting young women in natural settings. His works are characterized by their soft color palettes and delicate brushwork, capturing the essence of leisure and beauty.
alexandr-averin.o: Across all four renders, the style is richly painterly, with visible directional brushwork, luminous highlights, and layered color shaping faces, fabric, water, and flowers. It consistently presents romantic female figures in elaborate outdoor or interior garden settings, combining detailed floral surroundings with expressive, sunlit atmosphere and elegant clothing.

alexandre-benois.a: Alexandre Benois was a Russian artist, art critic, and stage designer, known for his influential role in the development of Russian art and theater in the early 20th century. He was a key figure in the Mir iskusstva (World of Art) movement and contributed significantly to the Ballets Russes, collaborating with renowned figures like Sergei Diaghilev.
alexandre-benois.o: Across all four images, the style uses richly textured, hand-painted-looking brushwork with loose directional strokes, layered washes, and finely observed architectural and environmental details. Muted, atmospheric palettes support narrative scenes populated by small figures, while dramatic lighting, strong silhouettes, and carefully framed vistas give the images an illustrative cinematic quality.

alexandre-cabanel.a: Alexandre Cabanel was a prominent French painter of the 19th century, known for his academic style and contributions to the Salon art exhibitions. He was celebrated for his mythological and historical subjects, often depicting idealized beauty and elegance. Cabanel's work is characterized by meticulous attention to detail, smooth brushwork, and a harmonious color palette, which made him a leading figure in the academic art movement.
alexandre-cabanel.o: Across the sheet, the style uses richly layered, visibly painted surfaces with fine brushwork, carefully modeled faces, and densely ornamented fabrics and accessories. Close-cropped figures are arranged in intimate, expressive groupings against dark grounds, with restrained jewel tones and warm highlights creating a classical, dramatic atmosphere.

alexandre-calame.a: Alexandre Calame was a Swiss painter known for his dramatic and detailed landscapes, particularly those depicting the Swiss Alps. Born in 1810, Calame became a prominent figure in the Romantic movement, capturing the grandeur and beauty of nature with precision and emotion. His works are celebrated for their meticulous attention to detail and ability to convey the sublime power of the natural world.
alexandre-calame.o: Across all four renders, the style presents expansive alpine landscapes with towering crags, glaciers, lakes, trees, and dramatic cloud formations. Richly textured, painterly surfaces combine vivid natural color with strong sunlight and shadow, producing a cinematic, dreamy sense of scale and epic atmosphere.

alexandre-deschaumes.a: Alexandre Deschaumes is a renowned French photographer known for his evocative and atmospheric landscape photography. His work often captures the ethereal beauty of nature, blending elements of fantasy and reality to create dreamlike scenes that evoke a sense of wonder and introspection.
alexandre-deschaumes.o: Across all four renders, the style presents vast, realistic mountain landscapes with monumental cliffs, deep valleys, and carefully resolved rocky and vegetation textures. Dark atmospheric palettes, strong light-and-shadow contrasts, drifting mist, and cinematic scale create an epic, dreamlike sense of wilderness.

alexandre-evariste-fragonard.a: Alexandre-Evariste Fragonard was a French painter and sculptor, known for his works that often depicted historical and mythological subjects. He was the son of the famous Rococo painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard, and his style was influenced by both the Rococo and Neoclassical movements, blending intricate details with classical themes.
alexandre-evariste-fragonard.o: The style uses richly textured, painterly landscapes with monumental cliffs, gnarled trees, clouds, and tiny human figures arranged for immense vertical scale. Deep shadow against luminous shafts of warm light, reflective water, and expressive gestures create an epic, theatrical fantasy atmosphere across the scenes.

alexei-harlamoff.a: Alexei Harlamoff was a Russian painter known for his exquisite portraits and genre scenes, often depicting young women and children with a focus on delicate beauty and emotional depth. His works are characterized by their fine brushwork, attention to detail, and use of light to create a soft, intimate atmosphere.
alexei-harlamoff.o: These images use richly visible, layered brushwork to model faces, hair, animals, and rough fabrics against nearly black grounds. Restrained earthy colors, candlelike warm highlights, deep shadows, and intimate close framing create an expressive, somber portrait-and-tableau style.

alexej-von-jawlensky.a: Alexej von Jawlensky was a Russian expressionist painter known for his vivid use of color and abstracted portraits. He was a key figure in the early 20th-century avant-garde movement and a member of the Blaue Reiter group, which played a significant role in the development of modern art.
alexej-von-jawlensky.o: Across all four renders, faces are reduced to boldly outlined, abstract planes of saturated color, with distorted features and cropped portrait framing. Visible brush marks and rough, built-up paint give the clean graphic shapes a strongly tactile, expressive surface.

alexey-brodovitch.a: Alexey Brodovitch was a Russian-born photographer, designer, and art director, best known for his work with Harper's Bazaar where he revolutionized magazine design with innovative layouts and typography. His influence extended to many areas of visual culture, including photography and graphic design, where his modernist approach left a lasting impact.
alexey-brodovitch.o: This style combines stark black-and-white portrait photography with geometric collage, obscuring and recombining faces through rectangular cutouts, overlays, and repeated eyes. Heavy shadows, grain, paper-like texture, bold graphic shapes, and occasional brush-edged circular framing create a severe, surreal editorial mood.

alfonso-cuaron.a: Alfonso Cuaron is a renowned Mexican filmmaker known for his diverse and impactful contributions to cinema. His works often explore themes of human connection, societal issues, and the fantastical, blending realism with imaginative storytelling. Cuaron's films, such as 'Gravity' and 'Roma,' have received critical acclaim for their innovative techniques and emotional depth.
alfonso-cuaron.o: The style is cinematic and photorealistic, using carefully staged narrative scenes, dramatic close-ups, and expansive environmental views. Deep shadows, teal-leaning darkness, warm isolated highlights, reflective surfaces, and luminous practical sources create a tense, surreal science-fiction atmosphere across the images.

alfred-augustus-glendening.a: Alfred Augustus Glendening was a British landscape painter known for his detailed and idyllic depictions of the English countryside during the Victorian era. His works often feature serene natural settings, capturing the tranquility and beauty of rural life with a focus on light and atmosphere.
alfred-augustus-glendening.o: The style uses richly painterly, visible brushwork to render lush garden landscapes with realistic figures, reflective ponds, abundant flowers, and layered foliage. Warm natural light, subdued earthy color, and dense environmental detail create tranquil, romantic scenes with a polished storybook quality.

alfred-cheney-johnston.a: Alfred Cheney Johnston was an American photographer known for his portraits of Ziegfeld Follies showgirls during the early 20th century. His work is characterized by its glamorous and theatrical style, capturing the essence of the Roaring Twenties with a focus on elegance and beauty.
alfred-cheney-johnston.o: The style is a monochrome photographic portrait series built around glamorous, carefully posed women in elaborate period-inspired clothing and accessories. Strong tonal contrast, selective focus, and visible grain create a dark, theatrical studio mood, while feathers, beads, sequins, and jewelry provide ornate surface detail.

alfred-dehodencq.a: Alfred Dehodencq is a 19th-century French painter known for his vivid and emotive depictions of historical and cultural scenes. His works often explore themes of romance, drama, and the exotic, drawing inspiration from his travels in Spain and North Africa. Dehodencq's paintings are characterized by their rich color palettes, dynamic compositions, and a keen attention to detail, reflecting the influence of Romanticism and Realism.
alfred-dehodencq.o: The style presents richly textured oil-paint scenes with visible fine brushwork, warm earthy color, strong light-dark modeling, and carefully rendered fabrics, architecture, and landscapes. Portraits and travel-like tableaux are framed as ornate museum paintings, combining dark interiors with sunlit North African settings and elaborate period clothing.

alfred-eisenstaedt.a: Alfred Eisenstaedt was a renowned German-born American photographer and photojournalist, best known for his candid and spontaneous photographs. He was a pioneer in the field of photojournalism and worked for Life magazine, capturing some of the most iconic images of the 20th century. His work is characterized by its ability to capture human emotion and everyday life, often in black and white.
alfred-eisenstaedt.o: The style is monochrome, high-contrast street photography with a grainy archival feel, shallow focus, and strong cinematic framing. Repeated foreground figures and spontaneous kissing poses create kinetic public scenes against dense skyscraper-lined avenues and gathered crowds.

alfred-guillou.a: Alfred Guillou is a French painter known for his realistic depictions of Breton life, particularly focusing on the daily activities and interactions of fishermen and their families. Born in 1844 in Concarneau, France, Guillou was a prominent figure in the 19th-century art scene, contributing to the genre of academic realism with his detailed and emotive works.
alfred-guillou.o: Across all four renders, the style is richly painterly, with visible directional brushwork modelling faces, fabric, water, and sky. Muted coastal colors, expressive figures, and active shoreline tasks create detailed, classical-looking maritime scenes with a soft atmospheric light.

alfred-henry-maurer.a: Alfred Henry Maurer was an American modernist painter known for his bold use of color and form. Born in 1868, Maurer initially worked in a traditional style but later embraced modernism, becoming one of the first American artists to adopt the avant-garde movements of the early 20th century. His work often featured expressive portraits and figures, characterized by a vivid color palette and dynamic compositions.
alfred-henry-maurer.o: Across all four portraits, thick visible paint marks build faces, clothing, furniture, and backgrounds with energetic variation in stroke direction. The style combines saturated reds, blues, greens, and whites with strong light-dark contrasts, presenting fashionable seated women in richly dressed, expressive poses.

alfred-hitchcock.a: Alfred Hitchcock was a renowned British filmmaker known for his mastery of suspense and psychological thrillers. He directed numerous iconic films such as "Psycho," "Vertigo," and "The Birds," which have left a lasting impact on the film industry. Hitchcock's work is characterized by its innovative use of camera angles, lighting, and narrative techniques to create tension and intrigue.
alfred-hitchcock.o: The style combines stark, high-contrast monochrome portraiture with heavily modelled faces, dark suits, and ravens, while one variation shifts into saturated red and green paint. Across the sheet, expressive distortions, close cropping, visible brush texture, and theatrical shadow make the imagery feel ominous and psychologically charged.

alfred-kubin.a: Alfred Kubin was an Austrian printmaker and illustrator known for his dark and fantastical imagery. Born in 1877, Kubin's work often explored themes of the macabre and surreal, reflecting the anxieties and existential concerns of his time. His style is characterized by intricate line work and a haunting atmosphere, drawing inspiration from both symbolism and expressionism.
alfred-kubin.o: Across all four renders, the style uses monochrome, heavily textured linework with fine hatching and ink-like shading to build stark, dreamlike scenes. Familiar forms such as birds, eyes, and human figures are distorted through unnatural scale and eerie juxtapositions, creating a surreal and ominous visual language.

alfred-munnings.a: Alfred Munnings was a renowned British painter known for his equestrian and landscape paintings. Born in 1878, Munnings became a leading figure in the British art scene, celebrated for his ability to capture the vitality and grace of horses. His works often depicted scenes of rural life and aristocratic leisure, reflecting the cultural and social milieu of early 20th-century England.
alfred-munnings.o: Across all four renders, the style is built from visible, energetic brushwork that models figures, horses, water, and landscape with layered, broken strokes. Restrained earth tones are punctuated by whites and reds, while strong light-dark contrasts and active mounted compositions create a dramatic, vigorous pictorial effect.

alfred-sisley.a: Alfred Sisley was a French Impressionist painter known for his landscape paintings that captured the serene beauty of the French countryside. Born in 1839, Sisley spent much of his life in France, where he developed a style characterized by delicate brushwork and a focus on natural light. His works often depict rivers, rural paths, and the changing seasons, reflecting a deep appreciation for nature.
alfred-sisley.o: These landscapes are rendered with clearly visible, varied brushwork that builds trees, clouds, water reflections, and architecture from luminous broken strokes. Bright blue skies, fresh greens, and warm highlights create an airy, sunlit atmosphere, while broad river views and small human activities give each image a tranquil sense of place.

alfred-stevens.a: Alfred Stevens was a Belgian painter known for his elegant depictions of women in domestic settings during the 19th century. He was associated with the Realism movement and often portrayed scenes of bourgeois life, capturing the fashion and interiors of the time with meticulous detail.
alfred-stevens.o: Across all four renders, richly painted interior scenes show elegantly dressed women surrounded by framed pictures, mirrors, furniture, and flowers. Visible directional brushwork builds the fabrics, faces, wood, and furnishings, while a restrained palette of deep reds, browns, blacks, creams, and muted floral accents creates a refined, intimate atmosphere.

alfred-stieglitz.a: Alfred Stieglitz was a pioneering American photographer and a key figure in the development of modern photography. He was instrumental in establishing photography as a recognized art form and was known for his contributions to the Photo-Secession movement. Stieglitz's work often focused on the interplay between the natural and urban environments, capturing the essence of early 20th-century America.
alfred-stieglitz.o: The style presents dramatic urban waterfront scenes in near-monochrome, with dense smoke, reflective water, and strongly backlit silhouettes creating stark tonal separation. Grain, atmospheric softness, period clothing, old vehicles, and monumental city architecture give the images a cinematic vintage-documentary appearance.

alfred-wallis.a: Alfred Wallis was a British fisherman and self-taught artist known for his distinctive naive style, depicting maritime scenes and landscapes. Born in 1855 in Devon, England, Wallis began painting in his later years, using materials like cardboard and household paint. His work is characterized by its simplicity, bold outlines, and flat perspective, capturing the essence of the Cornish coast and seafaring life.
alfred-wallis.o: Across all four renders, maritime scenes are built from simplified, strongly outlined boats, lighthouses, and clustered harbor buildings. Muted blue, cream, black, and umber hues sit on visibly worked paint surfaces, with broad marks, scraped texture, and aged crackle giving the illustrations a weathered, tactile finish.

alfredo-jaar.a: Alfredo Jaar is a Chilean-born artist and architect known for his thought-provoking installations and public interventions that often address social and political issues. His work frequently explores themes of media representation and the power dynamics inherent in the dissemination of information.
alfredo-jaar.o: The style is cinematic and realistic, presenting monumental contemporary interiors with strong geometric structure, deep perspective, and carefully balanced solitary figures. Dark industrial spaces are punctuated by luminous screens or bulbs, producing moody blue and amber palettes, strong contrast, reflective floors, and expansive negative space.

alice-bailly.a: Alice Bailly was a Swiss painter known for her vibrant and dynamic works that often incorporated elements of cubism and futurism. Her art is characterized by bold colors, fluid forms, and a sense of movement, capturing the energy of early 20th-century modernism.
alice-bailly.o: Across the sheet, figures and faces are built from sharply faceted geometric planes, strong dark contours, and carefully layered color fields. The images retain visible paint and canvas texture while combining vivid clothing and architectural colors with highly stylized, angular portraiture.

alice-kettle.a: Alice Kettle is a contemporary British textile artist known for her large-scale, expressive works that blend traditional embroidery techniques with modern artistic practices. Her art often explores themes of identity, nature, and human experience, utilizing intricate stitching and vibrant colors to create dynamic and textured pieces.
alice-kettle.o: The style combines intensely textured, hand-painted portraiture with assembled textile surfaces, frayed threads, woven fabric, and fine loose linework. Vivid reds, blues, greens, and oranges heighten the expressive faces and surreal narrative scenes, while collage-like layering makes the images feel tactile and materially constructed.

alice-neel.a: Alice Neel is a renowned American painter known for her distinctive portraits that capture the psychological depth and individuality of her subjects. Born in 1900, Neel's work often reflects the social and cultural dynamics of 20th-century America, with a focus on urban life and the human condition. Her expressive style and keen observation skills have made her a significant figure in modern art.
alice-neel.o: Across all four images, the style uses visibly worked paint with energetic directional strokes, strong contour accents, and layered color to build expressive faces, clothing, and interiors. Saturated blues, reds, and oranges contrast with dark neutrals, while tightly cropped family groupings and solitary seated figures create intimate, psychologically charged portraits.

alice-pasquini.a: Alice Pasquini is an Italian street artist known for her vibrant and expressive murals that often depict emotional and introspective themes. Her work is characterized by a focus on human figures, particularly women, and explores themes of connection, intimacy, and the human experience. Pasquini's art can be found on walls across the globe, where she uses a combination of spray paint and mixed media to create layered and textured compositions.
alice-pasquini.o: Across all four panels, expressive close-up portraits combine heavy black drawn contours with visibly broad, layered paint strokes and richly textured wall surfaces. Saturated teal, orange, ochre, blue, and red create a vivid street-mural effect, while poster fragments, graffiti, and overlapping marks give the compositions a collage-like urban character.

alice-pike-barney.a: Alice Pike Barney is an American painter known for her contributions to the cultural life of Washington, D.C., in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Her work often explored themes of femininity and beauty, and she was a prominent figure in the American art scene, promoting the arts and supporting other artists.
alice-pike-barney.o: Across all four portraits, visible directional brushwork builds faces, hair, flowers, feathers, and richly textured garments rather than clean graphic shapes. The subdued, dark palette is enlivened by expressive pinks, blues, and reds, while close cropping and decorative accessories give the portraits an elegant, ornamental character.

alice-rahon.a: Alice Rahon is a French-Mexican painter and poet associated with the Surrealist movement. Born in 1904, she became known for her dreamlike and fantastical works that often incorporated elements of mythology and folklore. Her art is characterized by a blend of surrealism and symbolism, creating a unique visual language that explores the subconscious and the mystical.
alice-rahon.o: Across the four images, richly textured paint and fine, visible brushwork build dense botanical, textile, and architectural detail. Saturated reds, teals, blues, and blacks create an ornate, moody jewel-toned world populated by elongated figures, strange costumes, and fantastical gardens.

alicja-kwade.a: Alicja Kwade is a contemporary artist known for her thought-provoking sculptures and installations that explore themes of perception, time, and reality. Her work often incorporates everyday materials transformed into enigmatic and surreal forms, challenging viewers to question their understanding of the physical world.
alicja-kwade.o: The style presents monumental rocks and architectural interiors with highly realistic textures, carefully controlled geometry, and a restrained earthy palette. Strong daylight creates crisp pools of illumination and deep shadows, while spacious compositions and sparse arrangements give the scenes a quiet, sculptural presence.

alida-akers.a: Alida Akers is an artist known for her vibrant and intricate depictions of nature, often blending elements of fantasy and realism. Her work is characterized by a detailed and painterly approach, with a focus on floral and natural themes that evoke a sense of whimsy and wonder.
alida-akers.o: Across all four renders, dense botanical imagery is built from vivid, saturated color, clearly visible painted strokes, and fine contour lines. Oversized flowers, layered foliage, and occasional distant garden or mountain landscapes create an exuberant, decorative style that combines illustrative flat shapes with richly textured painterly surfaces.

alighiero-boetti.a: Alighiero Boetti is an Italian conceptual artist known for his innovative approach to art, often incorporating elements of chance, order, and collaboration in his works. He was a prominent figure in the Arte Povera movement, which emphasized the use of simple materials and a focus on the conceptual aspects of art. Boetti's work often explored themes of duality, identity, and the passage of time.
alighiero-boetti.o: Across all four images, dense multicolored fragments form maps, letterforms, figures, animals, and symbolic arrangements in a highly layered visual field. Flat, angular shapes and emphatic dark outlines coexist with visibly rough, tactile paint and collage-like surface variation, producing a vivid, crowded, surreal patchwork aesthetic.

aline-kominsky-crumb.a: Aline Kominsky-Crumb is an American cartoonist and illustrator, best known for her autobiographical comics which explore themes of feminism, sexuality, and female identity. Born in 1948 in Long Island, New York, Kominsky-Crumb began her career in the underground comix movement of the 1970s. She was a founding member of the all-female comic book collective Wimmen's Comix and later collaborated with her husband, the renowned cartoonist Robert Crumb , on a series of comics including Dirty Laundry Comics and Self-Loathing Comics. Kominsky-Crumb's work is characterized by its raw, confessional style and its unflinching exploration of the complexities of her personal life. Her alter ego, "The Bunch," often serves as the protagonist of her stories, allowing her to examine her experiences as a woman, wife, and mother with humor and honesty. In addition to her work in comics, Kominsky-Crumb has also worked as an illustrator for various publications and has exhibited her artwork in galleries around the world. One of her most notable works is the graphic memoir Need More Love: A Graphic Memoir, which was published in 2007. The book chronicles her life from her childhood in the 1950s to her experiences in the counterculture movement of the 1960s and 1970s, and her subsequent career as an artist. Kominsky-Crumb's contribution to the field of comics and graphic novels has been recognized with numerous awards, including the Inkpot Award and the Harvey Award for Best Inker. Her work continues to be influential in the world of alternative comics and graphic storytelling.
aline-kominsky-crumb.o: The style uses highly detailed illustrative drawing with delicate black contours, dense crosshatching, and expressive facial features. Most panels are monochrome, while occasional clothing and background accents use vivid flat color; the images combine portrait closeups with lively, comic-like narrative scenes.

aline-smithson.a: Aline Smithson is a contemporary American photographer known for her fine art portraiture and conceptual photography. Her work often explores themes of identity, memory, and nostalgia, using a blend of traditional and digital techniques to create evocative and thought-provoking images.
aline-smithson.o: The style combines cinematic, highly staged portraiture with richly decorated interiors and pastoral settings, using elaborate costumes, antiques, flowers, birds, and patterned surfaces as visual motifs. Saturated reds and greens contrast with pale skies and dresses, while carefully composed tableaux and slightly uncanny juxtapositions create a dreamy, surreal editorial mood.

alisa-burke.a: Alisa Burke is a contemporary artist known for her vibrant and expressive art that often incorporates floral motifs and intricate patterns. Her work is characterized by a whimsical and imaginative style, blending elements of fantasy and surrealism with a focus on nature and femininity.
alisa-burke.o: Across all four renders, expressive close-up portraits combine visible paint, translucent washes, splatters, and dense fine black linework. Vivid coral, turquoise, pink, blue, and orange shapes collide with floral and fashion-like motifs, producing a richly layered mixed-media illustration with surreal decorative intrusions.

alison-bechdel.a: Alison Bechdel is an American cartoonist known for her long-running comic strip "Dykes to Watch Out For" and her graphic memoir "Fun Home," which explores themes of family, identity, and sexuality. Her work often delves into personal and societal issues, earning her critical acclaim and a significant place in the world of graphic storytelling.
alison-bechdel.o: Across all four renders, the style uses expressive drawn portraits with strong black contouring, ink-like linework, and dense crosshatched shading. It combines clean illustrative color in one scene with mostly monochrome sketch treatment elsewhere, placing thoughtful seated figures in richly furnished interiors and urban surroundings.

aliza-razell.a: Aliza Razell is a contemporary artist known for her imaginative and surreal photographic compositions. She often explores themes of mythology and fantasy, creating visually striking images that blend reality with dreamlike elements.
aliza-razell.o: The style uses cinematic, photorealistic compositions with solitary figures placed in expansive landscapes and exaggerated natural phenomena. Teal-blue atmospheric tones, selective red accents, soft haze, shallow focus, and flowing fabric create a dreamy surrealism, while wind, drifting seeds, clouds, and trailing garments provide a persistent sense of motion.

allan-kaprow.a: Allan Kaprow was an American artist known for pioneering the "Happenings" movement, which blurred the boundaries between art and life. His work often involved audience participation and emphasized the ephemeral nature of art. Kaprow's innovative approach to art-making challenged traditional art forms and inspired future generations of artists.
allan-kaprow.o: Across the sheet, the style combines expressive figurative and abstract imagery with visibly broad, layered brushwork, splatters, and forceful dark linework. Scenes are presented as dramatic gallery installations or large-scale artworks, using saturated reds, blues, yellows, and blacks alongside stark monochrome imagery and strong contrasts.

allan-sekula.a: Allan Sekula was an American photographer, writer, and critic known for his work that explored the intersections of social, economic, and political themes. His photography often focused on maritime industries, labor, and the impacts of globalization, using a documentary style to convey complex narratives about society and capitalism.
allan-sekula.o: The style uses realistic, cinematic photography with restrained warm tones, deep shadows, and a nostalgic vintage-film atmosphere. Carefully framed urban, industrial, and coastal scenes emphasize strong perspective, solitary figures, old cars, and layered presentation within books, frames, and gallery settings.

allie-brosh.a: Allie Brosh is an American author and artist, best known for her webcomic "Hyperbole and a Half." Her work is characterized by its humorous and candid storytelling, often depicting personal anecdotes and struggles with mental health. Brosh's unique style combines simple, childlike drawings with sharp, witty narratives, making her a beloved figure in the world of webcomics.
allie-brosh.o: The style uses vividly colored, flat illustrative shapes enclosed by thick, irregular black outlines. Crowded groups of bizarre, elongated characters have oversized eyes, toothy mouths, awkward anatomy, and expressive comic expressions, with occasional scribbled interior texture and surreal tropical backgrounds.

alma-thomas.a: Alma Thomas was an influential African American artist known for her vibrant abstract paintings. She was a key figure in the Washington Color School and made significant contributions to the world of modern art with her unique use of color and form. Her work often reflects themes of nature and space, characterized by bold, colorful patterns and a sense of movement.
alma-thomas.o: The style uses vivid, hand-painted rectangular marks arranged into dense grids, vertical bands, and concentric rings. Repetition and geometric organization dominate, while visible brush texture and slightly irregular edges keep the colorful abstract compositions tactile rather than mechanically flat.

alma-woodsey-thomas.a: Alma Woodsey Thomas was an influential African American painter known for her vibrant abstract works and as a prominent figure in the Washington Color School. Born in 1891, she became the first graduate of Howard University's art department and later a key figure in the civil rights movement, using her art to express themes of joy and beauty.
alma-woodsey-thomas.o: Across all four renders, the style is abstract and pattern-driven, built from vivid blocks, stripes, grids, and mosaic-like repeated marks. Thick, visibly worked paint and irregular edges give the surfaces a tactile, energetic quality rather than a clean graphic finish.

alois-arnegger.a: Alois Arnegger was an Austrian painter known for his landscape paintings, particularly those depicting the Alps and Mediterranean scenes. Born in 1879, Arnegger's work is characterized by its romantic and idyllic portrayal of nature, often featuring majestic mountains, serene lakes, and lush greenery. His paintings are celebrated for their detailed and realistic style, capturing the beauty and tranquility of natural landscapes.
alois-arnegger.o: Across all four renders, the style uses richly painted, naturalistic landscapes with finely resolved foliage, architecture, water, snow, and atmospheric distance. Warm sunlight and reflective surfaces create a cinematic, dreamlike grandeur, while delicate brushwork and classical scenic compositions balance intimate human moments with expansive vistas.

alphonse-bertillon.a: Alphonse Bertillon was a French police officer and biometrics researcher who developed anthropometry, a systematic method for identifying individuals based on physical measurements. His work laid the foundation for modern forensic science and criminal identification techniques.
alphonse-bertillon.o: The style uses dark, atmospheric cinematic imagery with a sepia-leaning monochrome palette, heavy grain, soft focus, and pronounced light-versus-shadow contrast. Portraits and woodland vignettes merge through ghostly double exposures, haze, backlighting, and luminous supernatural-looking overlays, creating a bleak surreal mood.

alphonse-mucha.a: Alphonse Mucha was a Czech painter and decorative artist known for his distinctive Art Nouveau style. His work, characterized by elegant compositions and intricate details, became iconic in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Mucha's art often featured beautiful women surrounded by elaborate floral patterns and ornate designs, capturing the essence of the Belle Époque era.
alphonse-mucha.o: Across all four renders, the style combines finely rendered female portraits with abundant flowers, flowing hair, circular medallion framing, and dense decorative borders. Muted earthy colors, delicate linework, and softly modeled painted surfaces create an elegant, highly ornamental botanical composition.

alphonse-osbert.a: Alphonse Osbert is a French Symbolist painter known for his ethereal landscapes and mystical themes. Born in 1857, Osbert's work often features serene, dreamlike settings with a focus on nature and solitude. His paintings are characterized by their soft color palettes and contemplative mood, reflecting the Symbolist movement's emphasis on emotion and spirituality.
alphonse-osbert.o: Across all four images, the style combines softly textured, visibly painted surfaces with highly composed illustrative scenes of solitary figures, trees, and water. A subdued, dusk-heavy palette contrasts deep silhouettes with warm amber light, while fine detail, patterned fabric, reflective lakes, and atmospheric woodland settings create a melancholic, dreamlike mood.

alson-skinner-clark.a: Alson Skinner Clark was an American Impressionist painter known for his landscapes, cityscapes, and depictions of urban life. Born in 1876, Clark studied art in Chicago and Paris, and his work often reflects the influence of French Impressionism. He is celebrated for his ability to capture light and atmosphere, particularly in scenes of Southern California and Europe.
alson-skinner-clark.o: Across all four images, the style is visibly oil-painted, with broad directional strokes, textured buildup, and expressive handling rather than clean graphic edges. It combines richly varied, often vivid color and strong light-dark contrast with detailed narrative scenes and portraits, presented as traditional framed paintings.

alvar-aalto.a: Alvar Aalto was a Finnish architect and designer, known for his significant contributions to modern architecture and design. He was a key figure in the development of Nordic modernism, blending functionality with organic forms and natural materials. Aalto's works often reflect a deep connection with nature, emphasizing harmony and simplicity.
alvar-aalto.o: The style presents architectural spaces as highly realistic, carefully composed photographs with strong geometric structure and sculptural curved forms. Warm natural light, subdued earthy colors, crisp material textures, and cinematic viewpoints consistently emphasize the buildings’ relationship with surrounding trees, sky, paths, and landscaped grounds.

alvaro-castagnet.a: Alvaro Castagnet is a renowned Uruguayan watercolor artist known for his vibrant and expressive style. He has gained international acclaim for his ability to capture the essence of a scene with bold brushstrokes and a vivid color palette. Castagnet's work often features urban landscapes and figures, rendered with a dynamic and fluid approach that emphasizes light and atmosphere.
alvaro-castagnet.o: Across the portraits and city views, the style combines visibly layered, directional paintwork with cinematic framing and dense architectural detail. Subdued blue-gray surroundings are punctuated by intense orange-red lights, reflected across wet streets and softened by mist, creating a dark, atmospheric urban mood.

alvaro-siza.a: Alvaro Siza is a renowned Portuguese architect known for his modernist and minimalist designs. His work is characterized by clean lines, functional forms, and a deep respect for the surrounding environment. Siza's architecture often integrates seamlessly with its context, reflecting a thoughtful balance between innovation and tradition.
alvaro-siza.o: The style presents monumental modern architecture as crisp, realistic architectural photography, emphasizing geometric planes, sculptural massing, stairways, and deep spatial recesses. Warm pale concrete, saturated blue skies, strong sunlight, and pronounced shadows create a restrained but high-contrast atmosphere, with small human figures reinforcing the scale.

alvin-langdon-coburn.a: Alvin Langdon Coburn was an influential American photographer known for his pioneering work in the early 20th century. He was a key figure in the Pictorialist movement, which emphasized the artistic aspects of photography. Coburn's work often featured soft focus and atmospheric effects, capturing urban landscapes and portraits with a unique sense of mood and depth.
alvin-langdon-coburn.o: The style uses monochrome, sepia-tinged photographic imagery with heavy grain, deep shadows, and stark backlighting. Fog and soft focus dissolve city architecture into atmospheric silhouettes, while intimate figures, water, streets, and winter trees create a cinematic, melancholic urban mood.

alvin-lustig.a: Alvin Lustig is an influential American graphic designer known for his innovative approach to book cover design and typography during the mid-20th century. His work is characterized by a modernist aesthetic, combining abstract forms with bold color palettes. Lustig's designs have left a lasting impact on the field of graphic design, particularly in the areas of visual communication and branding.
alvin-lustig.o: Across the sheet, the style uses graphic flat-color forms, heavy black contours, geometric patterning, and strongly limited but saturated red, orange, blue, cream, and black. Repeated facial motifs and sharply framed portrait silhouettes are treated like retro print compositions, with a consistent grainy paper or screenprint texture and stark contrast.

alyssa-monks.a: Alyssa Monks is a contemporary American painter known for her hyperrealistic portraits that often incorporate water and glass to create a sense of distortion and intimacy. Her work explores themes of identity, emotion, and the human experience, using oil paint to achieve a striking level of detail and realism.
alyssa-monks.o: The style presents intensely cropped, near-photorealistic faces with highly visible skin, hair, water, and droplet detail. Cool, restrained colors, dramatic contrast, and tactile painterly marks create an intimate, emotionally charged effect, while the fragmented multi-face arrangements lend the portraits a surreal quality.

amanda-blake.a: Amanda Blake is a contemporary artist known for her whimsical and surreal paintings that often feature elongated figures and dreamlike settings. Her work is characterized by a blend of fantasy and reality, creating a unique narrative style that draws viewers into a world of imagination and emotion.
amanda-blake.o: The style combines childlike, front-facing portraiture with softly distorted proportions, oversized eyes, rosy cheeks, and simplified facial features. Visible brushwork and thickly built paint create a tactile surface, while muted pastel pinks, creams, reds, and blue-grays support floral clothing, bouquets, and whimsical character groupings.

amanda-clark.a: Amanda Clark is a contemporary artist known for her enchanting and whimsical illustrations that often draw inspiration from nature and folklore. Her work is characterized by a dreamy and fantastical style, blending elements of surrealism and detailed floral motifs.
amanda-clark.o: Across all four images, richly textured paint and delicate visible marks build dense woodland scenes filled with flowers, trees, animals, and fairy-tale figures. The recurring blue-green atmosphere, selective red accents, intricate botanical patterning, and softly strange encounters give the style a dreamy, ornate storybook quality.

amanda-sage.a: Amanda Sage is a contemporary visionary artist known for her intricate and detailed paintings that often explore themes of spirituality and consciousness. Her work is characterized by a unique blend of surrealism and fantasy, often incorporating vibrant colors and complex patterns. Sage's art invites viewers into a world of introspection and mystical exploration, reflecting her deep interest in the interconnectedness of life.
amanda-sage.o: The style combines highly detailed botanical forms with expressive human faces, fusing skin, leaves, veins, tendrils, and floral structures into dense organic compositions. Saturated orange, purple, teal, and green hues, crisp fine linework, and decorative surface patterning create an ornate, surreal fantasy illustration language.

amandine-van-ray.a: Amandine van Ray is a contemporary digital artist known for her ethereal and surreal portraits that blend fantasy with delicate realism. Her work often features young women adorned with intricate floral arrangements and dreamlike elements, creating a sense of whimsical beauty and tranquility.
amandine-van-ray.o: The style presents highly realistic, cinematic tableaux with expressive figures in flowing ivory garments, set against misty forests or dramatic cloudscapes. Subdued green, cream, and grey tones, soft atmospheric light, elaborate fabric texture, and mythic human-animal encounters create a dreamy, epic fantasy mood.

ambient-lighting.a: Ambient lighting is a type of lighting that provides overall illumination to a space, creating a uniform level of light without highlighting any particular area. It is often used to establish a comfortable and inviting atmosphere in various settings, such as homes, offices, and public spaces. This lighting style is typically achieved through ceiling fixtures, wall sconces, or floor lamps, and it plays a crucial role in interior design by enhancing the mood and functionality of a room.
ambient-lighting.o: The style presents realistic, carefully composed interior spaces with strong geometric architecture, restrained earthy materials, and abundant sculptural furnishings. Warm pools of lamp light and concealed illumination create a dark, moody atmosphere, while repeated vertical slats, clean planes, and uncluttered arrangements give the rooms a refined modern character.

ambrogio-lorenzetti.a: Ambrogio Lorenzetti was an Italian painter active during the early 14th century, known for his contributions to the Sienese School and the development of early Renaissance art. His works often depicted religious themes and civic allegories, characterized by their detailed narrative style and use of perspective.
ambrogio-lorenzetti.o: The style uses finely rendered, visibly aged paint with delicate linework, restrained earth-and-sky colors, and densely described figures, architecture, and foliage. Formal compositions combine religious or courtly vignettes with expansive townscapes, using elongated forms, patterned surfaces, and repeated arches and towers.

ambrosius-benson.a: Ambrosius Benson is a Flemish painter from the Renaissance period, known for his detailed portraits and religious works. He was active in the early 16th century and is associated with the Northern Renaissance movement, contributing significantly to the art scene in Bruges with his refined technique and elegant compositions.
ambrosius-benson.o: The style presents tightly cropped, highly realistic painted portraits and figure groups with exceptionally careful rendering of faces, hands, feathers, fur, and woven fabrics. Dark grounds and strong light-dark separation make the subdued reds, browns, blacks, and pale flesh tones especially prominent, while fine brushwork and a subtly aged surface give the images a richly finished, historical appearance.

ambrosius-bosschaert.a: Ambrosius Bosschaert was a Dutch painter known for his exquisite still life paintings, particularly those featuring flowers. He was a pioneer in the genre of floral still life during the Dutch Golden Age , and his works are celebrated for their meticulous detail and vibrant color.
ambrosius-bosschaert.o: Across all four renders, densely layered flower arrangements are painted with delicate, visible brushwork and realistic petal and foliage modeling. Restrained jewel-like reds, oranges, whites, pinks, and blues emerge from near-black grounds, producing strong contrast and an ornate, antique still-life appearance.

amedeo-modigliani.a: Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian painter and sculptor known for his distinctive style characterized by elongated forms, simplified shapes, and a focus on portraits. Born in 1884, Modigliani became a prominent figure in the early 20th-century Parisian art scene, contributing to the modernist movement with his unique approach to form and color.
amedeo-modigliani.o: Across all four portraits, simplified elongated faces, almond-shaped eyes, angular noses, and strong contour lines create a stylized, graphic character. Richly textured brushwork remains visible throughout, combining muted earthy backgrounds with concentrated red, blue, black, and flesh tones and carefully posed fashion details.

american-girl-doll.a: American Girl doll is a line of 18-inch dolls created by Pleasant Company in 1986, known for their historical and contemporary characters that represent various periods and cultures in American history. Each doll comes with a story that educates children about different eras and experiences, often accompanied by books and accessories.
american-girl-doll.o: The style uses highly realistic, detailed close-up portrait photography of dolls, with glossy glass eyes, finely rendered synthetic hair, skin texture, and carefully patterned clothing. Warm vivid colors, soft daylight, and shallow focus isolate each doll against gently blurred backgrounds while preserving a tactile, lifelike toy appearance.

ami-james.a: Ami James is a renowned tattoo artist known for his bold and intricate designs. He gained fame through his appearances on reality TV shows focused on tattoo artistry, where his skill and distinctive style were showcased to a wide audience. James is recognized for his contributions to the tattoo industry and his ability to blend traditional and modern elements in his work.
ami-james.o: The style combines realistic close-up photography with highly detailed illustrative tattoo designs, defined by crisp black contour lines, dense ornamental imagery, and saturated red, teal, blue, and orange accents. Portraits and body details are framed tightly, with selective focus and strong contrast emphasizing the tattoos as bold, layered compositions on skin.

amigurumi.a: Amigurumi is a Japanese art form that involves knitting or crocheting small, stuffed yarn creatures. Typically, these creations are characterized by their cute and whimsical appearance, often depicting animals or fantasy characters with exaggerated features like large eyes and rounded shapes.
amigurumi.o: The style presents charming crocheted character toys with highly legible yarn stitches, rounded forms, oversized glossy eyes, and whimsical animal-like features. It combines colorful illustrative character design with softly photographed settings, selective focus, and varied group arrangements against natural or simple studio backgrounds.

amrita-sher-gil.a: Amrita Sher-Gil was an influential Indian painter, often considered a pioneer of modern Indian art. Born in 1913 in Hungary, she was known for her expressive and evocative portrayal of Indian women and rural life. Her work is celebrated for its fusion of Western and Indian artistic traditions, and she is often compared to Frida Kahlo for her bold and introspective style.
amrita-sher-gil.o: The style uses richly textured, visibly hand-painted surfaces with fine, controlled brushwork, warm earthy reds, browns, creams, and deep greens. It focuses on elegantly posed women in tightly framed portrait groupings, combining carefully rendered facial features, garments, jewelry, and decorative textile backgrounds.

amy-brown.a: Amy Brown is a contemporary American fantasy artist known for her whimsical and enchanting fairy illustrations. Her work often features delicate, ethereal figures set in magical landscapes, drawing inspiration from folklore and nature.
amy-brown.o: Across all four renders, richly layered woodland scenes combine graceful fairy-like figures with animals, dense foliage, flowers, berries, mushrooms, and rocky natural forms. Fine drawn contours and visible painted texture create highly detailed, ornate imagery in an earthy, subdued palette, with a dreamy fantasy atmosphere and expressive flowing hair and garments.

amy-earles.a: Amy Earles is an artist known for her intricate and whimsical illustrations that often explore themes of fantasy and the surreal. Her work is characterized by a blend of gothic and fairy tale elements, creating a unique and enchanting visual style.
amy-earles.o: Across all four images, finely rendered figures and animals occupy richly patterned woodland scenes, with visible brush texture, delicate linework, and ornamental clothing and foliage. The restrained beige, charcoal, cream, and red palette creates strong dark-light separation and a consistently shadowed, gothic mood.

amy-giacomelli.a: Amy Giacomelli is a contemporary artist known for her vibrant and whimsical paintings that often incorporate elements of nature and fantasy. Her work is characterized by intricate detailing and a playful use of color, creating a sense of movement and life within her compositions.
amy-giacomelli.o: Across all four renders, the style uses visible, swirling brushwork to build richly textured skies, clouds, foliage, and ground, with expressive red-orange and blue color contrasts. Monumental autumn trees, moons, and branching silhouettes create dreamlike landscape compositions that balance detailed natural forms with deliberately stylized, patterned surfaces.

amy-judd.a: Amy Judd is a contemporary artist known for her ethereal and surreal portraits that often blend human forms with elements of nature. Her work explores themes of femininity and fantasy, creating a unique visual language that captivates viewers with its delicate and dreamlike quality.
amy-judd.o: The style uses highly realistic, finely rendered portraiture with dense feather textures treated as extravagant sculptural garments and headpieces. Restrained blue, ivory, skin, and occasional deep red create a dreamlike surreal mood, while repeated doves and obscured eyes give the compositions a theatrical, symbolic quality.

amy-sherald.a: Amy Sherald is an American painter known for her distinctive portraits that explore themes of race and identity. Her work often features African American subjects depicted in a stylized, surreal manner with a focus on individuality and cultural pride. Sherald gained widespread recognition for her official portrait of former First Lady Michelle Obama, which exemplifies her unique approach to portraiture.
amy-sherald.o: The style uses graphic, poster-like portraiture with vivid complementary colours, hard-edged shapes, and strongly simplified dark figures. Repeated stripes, checks, dots, foliage, hats, headwraps, and elaborate garments create an ornamental fashion-editorial language across the portraits, while high contrast keeps facial features and silhouettes striking.

amy-sillman.a: Amy Sillman is an American contemporary artist known for her vibrant and dynamic abstract paintings. Her work often explores themes of color, form, and gesture, blending elements of abstraction with figuration. Sillman's art is characterized by its bold use of color, expressive brushwork, and a playful yet contemplative approach to composition.
amy-sillman.o: Across all four renders, the style uses layered, visibly brushed paint with large interlocking geometric fragments, translucent washes, and energetic hand-drawn contour lines. Saturated oranges, blues, greens, pinks, and dark neutrals alternate with pale grounds, creating an expressive abstract collage-like surface that balances flat color fields against tactile texture.

amy-sol.a: Amy Sol is a contemporary artist known for her ethereal and whimsical paintings, often depicting young women in dreamlike settings. Her work is characterized by soft, muted color palettes and delicate, illustrative linework, drawing inspiration from nature and fantasy themes.
amy-sol.o: The style combines highly detailed, softly painterly female portraits with ornate botanical and avian motifs. Muted sage, cream, charcoal, and rust tones, delicate linework, flowing hair, and carefully arranged floral or branch-like framing create a dreamy, romantic fantasy atmosphere across the set.

ana-mendieta.a: Ana Mendieta was a Cuban-American artist known for her groundbreaking work in performance art, land art, and body art. Her art often explored themes of identity, feminism, and spirituality, using natural materials and her own body as mediums. Mendieta's work is characterized by its deep connection to nature and its exploration of cultural and ancestral roots.
ana-mendieta.o: A realistic, cinematic photographic style built around vivid rust-red clothing and wet earth, with strong contrast between illuminated skin, dark hair, and heavy clay textures. Intimate close-ups alternate with posed full-body compositions, producing an expressive, bold, and slightly dark editorial mood.

anaglyph.a: Anaglyph is a stereoscopic 3D effect that uses color filters, typically red and cyan, to create a perception of depth in images. This technique has been historically used in photography and film to provide a three-dimensional viewing experience when viewed with corresponding colored glasses.
anaglyph.o: Across the portraits, figure studies, and sculptural forms, the style combines vivid red⁠–cyan color separation with deep shadows and assertive graphic lighting. Broad, visibly textured brushwork and rough surfaces give the imagery an expressive, tactile quality, while oversized geometric forms and displaced color edges create a surreal, digitally warped mood.

anaglyph-colors.a: Anaglyph colors is a technique used to create 3D images by encoding each eye's image using filters of usually red and cyan. When viewed through glasses with corresponding colored lenses, the images appear three-dimensional.
anaglyph-colors.o: Across all four renders, recognizable faces and organic forms dissolve into energetic, radiating streaks and viscous, painterly distortions. The style is defined by intensely saturated cyan, red, magenta, and blue, strong dark-light separation, luminous internal highlights, and persistent red-cyan displacement that gives the imagery a surreal, kinetic feel.

anato-finnstark.a: Anato Finnstark is a contemporary digital artist known for his evocative and fantastical illustrations that blend elements of surrealism and dark fantasy. His work often explores mythical themes and cosmic landscapes, creating immersive worlds that captivate the imagination.
anato-finnstark.o: Across all four images, visible brushwork, softened edges, and layered texture create a painterly, expressive storybook atmosphere. Dark blue, brown, and rust tones dominate, with stark pale figures and localized fiery light producing dramatic contrast, while recurring characters, birds, forests, and monumental settings give the style a surreal dark-fantasy character.

anatoly-metlan.a: Anatoly Metlan is a contemporary artist known for his vibrant and expressive paintings, often depicting scenes of leisure and beauty. His work is characterized by a rich use of color and dynamic compositions that capture moments of elegance and tranquility.
anatoly-metlan.o: Across all four renders, the style uses vivid, sunlit color and visible directional brushwork to build richly textured coastal scenes. Elegant figures in flowing dresses and wide-brimmed hats are integrated with harbors, terraces, villas, flowers, and reflective water through expressive, painterly detail.

anatomical-illustration.a: Anatomical illustration is a detailed and precise form of art used to visually represent the structures of the human body. Historically, it has played a crucial role in medical education and scientific research, providing a clear and accurate depiction of anatomical features for students, doctors, and researchers. These illustrations are often characterized by their meticulous attention to detail and accuracy, serving as essential tools in understanding human anatomy.
anatomical-illustration.o: The style combines highly detailed anatomical portraiture with fine ink lines, dense crosshatching, and precise construction marks. Repeated side-profile figures merge flesh, bone, organs, and branching vessels into surreal compositions, shifting between restrained monochrome studies and sharply contrasted blue-red color treatments on a paper-like ground.

ancient-egyptian-mural.a: Ancient Egyptian mural is a form of art that adorned the walls of tombs and temples, serving both decorative and religious purposes. These murals often depicted scenes of daily life, mythology, and the afterlife, using a combination of painting and carving techniques. The art was characterized by its use of hierarchical proportions, where the size of figures indicated their importance, and a strict adherence to a grid system that maintained consistency in proportions and poses.
ancient-egyptian-mural.o: Across all four renders, the style presents densely decorated Egyptian temple or tomb interiors filled with hieroglyphs, ritual figures, offering scenes, and symbolic motifs. It combines weathered, visible wall texture and painterly pigment variation with precise fine outlines, flattened profile-based figures, restrained earthy colors, and highly ornamental surface detail.

anders-petersen.a: Anders Petersen is a renowned Swedish photographer known for his intimate and raw documentary style. His work often explores human relationships and urban life, capturing the essence of subcultures with a distinctive emotional depth. Petersen's photography is characterized by its high-contrast black and white imagery, often focusing on the gritty and unpolished aspects of life.
anders-petersen.o: Across all four renders, the style uses stark black-and-white photography with deep shadows, bright point lights, visible grain, and selective focus. Intimate close portraits of women in a dim bar are framed through reflections and foreground obstructions, producing a candid, nocturnal, cinematic mood.

anders-zorn.a: Anders Zorn is a renowned Swedish painter known for his masterful portraits and genre scenes, particularly those depicting the natural beauty and cultural life of his native Sweden. Born in 1860, Zorn's work is celebrated for its impressionistic style, characterized by loose brushwork and a keen attention to the effects of light and shadow. He gained international acclaim for his ability to capture the essence of his subjects with both realism and emotional depth.
anders-zorn.o: Across all four renders, the style is built from visible, directional paint strokes that model faces, fabric, foliage, and water with a richly textured surface. Warm ochres, creams, browns, blacks, and muted reds create a subdued, moody palette with strong light-dark separation, while cropped social scenes and portraits emphasize elegant figures, gestures, and atmospheric settings.

ando-fuchs.a: Ando Fuchs is a contemporary photographer known for his evocative black and white imagery that often explores themes of solitude and mystery within urban environments. His work is characterized by a strong sense of narrative and atmosphere, often drawing comparisons to the film noir genre and the works of classic photographers like Henri Cartier-Bresson.
ando-fuchs.o: Across all four renders, the style is monochrome, filmic, and strongly contrast-driven, using monumental urban architecture to frame solitary silhouetted figures. Dense fog, selective focus, grain, wet surfaces, and blown-out openings create a bleak, noir-like atmosphere with recurring deep shadows and luminous distant space.

andre-charles-boulle.a: Andre-Charles Boulle was a renowned French cabinetmaker and designer, celebrated for his mastery in marquetry and inlay techniques during the late 17th and early 18th centuries. Known for his innovative use of materials such as brass, tortoiseshell, and pewter, Boulle's work epitomizes the opulent style of the Louis XIV era, often featuring intricate designs and luxurious finishes.
andre-charles-boulle.o: The style presents highly ornate black lacquer furniture with dense floral inlay, elaborate scrollwork, sculpted gilded mounts, and strongly curved legs. Restrained black, red, and gold colors create a luxurious, high-detail appearance, while the clean studio staging and frontal views keep the objects legible and product-like.

andre-courreges.a: Andre Courreges was a French fashion designer known for his innovative and futuristic designs during the 1960s. He played a pivotal role in the space age fashion movement, introducing bold geometric shapes, monochrome palettes, and a minimalist aesthetic. Courreges's work was characterized by its forward-thinking approach and a departure from traditional fashion norms, often incorporating unconventional materials and styles.
andre-courreges.o: The style combines highly realistic, polished fashion photography with graphic, geometric silhouettes and deliberately futuristic retro styling. Saturated teal, white, orange, and red create bold blocks of color, while sculptural hats, glossy garments, sunglasses, and sparse architectural backdrops give the portraits a controlled editorial look.

andre-de-dienes.a: Andre de Dienes was a Hungarian-American photographer known for his work in fashion and glamour photography during the mid-20th century. He gained prominence for his portraits of Marilyn Monroe and other iconic figures of the era, capturing the essence of Hollywood glamour and beauty. His work often featured a blend of natural settings and intimate poses, creating a unique and recognizable style.
andre-de-dienes.o: A monochrome, high-contrast photographic style combines expressive fashion portraiture with spontaneous movement by the sea. Grain, shallow focus, windblown hair and fabric, dramatic cropping, and bright natural light give the images a cinematic editorial energy.

andre-derain.a: Andre Derain was a French artist and a key figure in the Fauvist movement, known for his bold use of color and expressive brushwork. Born in 1880, Derain's work was characterized by vibrant landscapes and a unique approach to color that broke away from traditional representation, influencing modern art.
andre-derain.o: Across all four renders, the style uses visibly built-up paint with broad, directional strokes, simplified yet strongly outlined forms, and vivid blue, coral, orange, cream, and deep green contrasts. It repeatedly depicts sunlit coastal and hillside landscapes with clustered architecture, water, trees, and occasional human activity, combining graphic structure with expressive, textured brushwork.

andre-franquin.a: André Franquin is a renowned Belgian comic artist best known for his work on the Spirou et Fantasio series and the creation of the character Gaston Lagaffe. His style is characterized by its humor, dynamic compositions, and expressive characters, making significant contributions to the Franco-Belgian comic tradition.
andre-franquin.o: The style combines expressive comic characters and adventurous action scenes with loose, energetic ink drawing, fine contour lines, splashes, and dense hatching. Most images use a restrained cream, black, and gray palette, with occasional muted blue and rust-red color, while exaggerated poses and sweeping marks create strong motion.

andre-kertesz.a: Andre Kertesz was a Hungarian-born photographer known for his groundbreaking contributions to photographic composition and the photo essay. His work is celebrated for its innovative use of angles and perspectives, capturing the essence of everyday life with a unique, often surreal vision. Kertesz's influence extends across generations, impacting the fields of photojournalism and art photography.
andre-kertesz.o: Across all four renders, the style uses stark black-and-white photography with hard sunlight, deep shadows, and strongly silhouetted figures. Elevated viewpoints, elongated cast shadows, and carefully staged urban situations create a dramatic, filmic documentary mood.

andre-kohn.a: Andre Kohn is a contemporary artist known for his expressive and elegant figurative paintings. His work often focuses on capturing the grace and beauty of the human form, particularly in moments of quiet reflection and solitude. Kohn's style is characterized by a blend of realism and impressionism, using fine brushstrokes and a rich, earthy color palette to create intimate and contemplative scenes.
andre-kohn.o: Across all four renders, the scenes use visibly built-up paint with broad, directional strokes, scraped textures, and loose expressive edges. Rainy urban settings, cropped pedestrians, umbrellas, and reflective pavement recur in a restrained cream-and-brown ground punctuated by vivid red accents, giving the fashion-focused street tableaux a dynamic, dreamlike quality.

andre-lhote.a: Andre Lhote was a French painter and sculptor known for his contributions to Cubism and his role as an influential art teacher. Born in 1885, Lhote's work often explored the boundaries between abstraction and representation, incorporating geometric shapes and vivid colors. He was a prominent figure in the early 20th-century art scene, contributing to the development of modern art through both his paintings and his teachings.
andre-lhote.o: Across all four renders, recognizable figures and domestic objects are built from angular, faceted shapes with strong dark contours and saturated ochre, red, blue, and teal color blocks. Broad visible brushstrokes and a built-up painted surface give the scenes tactile weight, while geometric simplification and expressive poses keep the imagery graphic rather than naturalistic.

andre-masson.a: Andre Masson is a French artist known for his contributions to Surrealism and Abstract Expressionism. His work often explores themes of the subconscious, mythology, and the human condition, utilizing automatic drawing techniques and biomorphic forms. Masson's art is characterized by its fluid lines, dynamic compositions, and symbolic imagery, reflecting his interest in psychoanalysis and dream interpretation.
andre-masson.o: Across all four renders, energetic gestural brushwork builds dense abstract compositions from biomorphic shapes, splatters, drips, and curling lines. Vivid coral, turquoise, yellow, pink, and black pigments create strong contrast, while recognizable hints of eyes, faces, petals, and creatures dissolve into surreal, kinetic patterning.

andrea-galvani.a: Andrea Galvani is an Italian contemporary artist known for his conceptual approach to photography and installation art. His work often explores themes of memory, time, and the intersection of science and art, using a mix of photography, drawing, and sculpture to create thought-provoking pieces.
andrea-galvani.o: The style uses photorealistic, cinematic wide compositions that place tiny solitary figures against immense landscapes and monumental cloud formations. Strong scale contrast, expansive negative space, soft natural light, and surreal juxtapositions make the scenes feel epic and otherworldly.

andrea-kowch.a: Andrea Kowch is a contemporary American painter known for her narrative style that often combines elements of magic realism and American Gothic. Her works frequently explore themes of solitude and introspection, set against the backdrop of rural American landscapes. Kowch's paintings are characterized by their meticulous detail and evocative storytelling, often featuring strong female figures in expansive natural settings.
andrea-kowch.o: Across all four renders, the style combines convincingly realistic figures with visible, finely worked paint texture and carefully described clothing, vegetation, and weathered rural settings. Muted earthy colors, overcast light, solemn expressions, and close portrait-like framing create a melancholy, filmic visual atmosphere.

andrea-mantegna.a: Andrea Mantegna was an Italian Renaissance painter known for his mastery of perspective and detail. Born in 1431, he was a prominent figure in the Italian Renaissance , contributing significantly to the development of illusionistic painting. Mantegna's work is characterized by its classical themes, meticulous attention to detail, and innovative use of perspective, which influenced many artists of his time.
andrea-mantegna.o: The style presents tightly cropped, highly rendered painted faces and figures with expressive gazes, tactile skin, hair, fabric, and metal surfaces. Earthy reds, browns, creams, and muted blues combine with strong light-dark modelling, visible fine brushwork, and an aged cracked-paint surface.

andrea-palladio.a: Andrea Palladio was a renowned Italian architect of the Renaissance , known for his influential designs and architectural treatises. His work, characterized by classical Roman principles, has left a lasting impact on Western architecture, giving rise to the Palladian style. Palladio's designs are celebrated for their symmetry, perspective, and harmonious proportions, drawing inspiration from ancient Roman architecture.
andrea-palladio.o: The style presents monumental classical architecture with carefully structured, often axial compositions, emphasizing domes, columns, pediments, arches, sculpture, and staircases. It combines restrained stone and sepia tones with finely drawn contours, architectural precision, and lightly weathered illustrative surfaces.

andrea-torres-balaguer.a: Andrea Torres Balaguer is a contemporary Spanish photographer known for her surreal and conceptual imagery. Her work often explores themes of identity, nature, and the subconscious, using a blend of photography and digital manipulation to create dreamlike scenes.
andrea-torres-balaguer.o: The style uses realistic, cinematic portrait photography with subdued, moody color grading, soft natural light, and shallow focus. Obscured faces, formal dark clothing, symbolic props, and carefully staged outdoor or interior settings create a dreamy, dark, psychologically charged atmosphere.

andreas-achenbach.a: Andreas Achenbach was a prominent German landscape painter of the 19th century, known for his dramatic and detailed depictions of natural scenes, particularly seascapes and coastal landscapes. He was a key figure in the Düsseldorf school of painting and contributed significantly to the Romantic movement in art.
andreas-achenbach.o: Across all four renders, the style uses richly textured painterly surfaces, dense environmental detail, and dramatic storm lighting to create immense, perilous coastal landscapes. Deep blue-green shadows, warm breaks of sunlight, rolling surf, mist, and monumental ruins give the scenes an epic fantasy atmosphere.

andreas-feininger.a: Andreas Feininger was a renowned American photographer known for his striking black and white images of urban landscapes, particularly New York City. Born in 1906, Feininger was celebrated for his ability to capture the architectural beauty and dynamic energy of city life. His work is characterized by a strong sense of composition, often employing high contrast and dramatic lighting to emphasize the geometric forms of skyscrapers and the bustling activity of urban environments.
andreas-feininger.o: Across all four renders, the style uses stark black-and-white photography with deep shadows, bright backlight, visible grain, and strong architectural geometry. Urban scenes are framed from dramatic low or receding viewpoints, with silhouetted figures and buildings creating a dark, cinematic documentary mood.

andreas-franke.a: Andreas Franke is an Austrian photographer known for his innovative and surreal underwater photography. He often combines elements of fantasy and reality to create dreamlike scenes that challenge perceptions and evoke a sense of wonder. His work frequently explores themes of isolation and beauty within decayed or submerged settings, capturing the imagination of viewers worldwide.
andreas-franke.o: The style presents highly detailed, realistic cinematic tableaux of grand interiors submerged beneath water, combining decaying architecture, furniture, plants, books, fish and elegantly posed figures. Deep teal-green tones, shafts of underwater light, glowing particulate bubbles and atmospheric haze create a moody surreal sense of suspended time.

andreas-gursky.a: Andreas Gursky is a renowned German photographer known for his large-scale, high-resolution images that capture the complexity and vastness of contemporary landscapes and architecture. His work often explores themes of globalization, consumerism, and the human impact on the environment, using a detached and analytical approach to document the world.
andreas-gursky.o: The style uses highly realistic, cinematic scenes with monumental scale, strong geometric architecture, and dense environmental detail. A restrained, slightly moody palette, atmospheric distance, and carefully staged gallery-like compositions recur across the mountain market, library, industrial city, and museum views, giving ordinary spaces a surreal sense of enormity.

andreas-levers.a: Andreas Levers is a contemporary photographer known for his evocative urban landscapes and atmospheric compositions. His work often explores themes of solitude and the interplay of light and shadow in modern environments, capturing the essence of urban life with a distinctive style.
andreas-levers.o: The style is cinematic and realistic, using restrained teal shadows against concentrated red-orange practical lights. Dense fog softens the urban architecture and creates layered depth, while wet streets, isolated figures, and strong pools of illumination give the scenes a dark, atmospheric mood.

andreas-rocha.a: Andreas Rocha is a contemporary digital artist known for his captivating fantasy landscapes and atmospheric scenes. His work often features intricate details and a strong sense of mood, drawing inspiration from fantasy literature and medieval themes.
andreas-rocha.o: The style presents vast, cinematic fantasy landscapes with highly realistic rocky terrain, monumental peaks, waterfalls, castles, and mountain settlements. Cool blue atmospheric shadows contrast with warm sunset or torchlight accents, while mist, dramatic clouds, and towering forms create an epic, dreamlike sense of scale.

andreas-vesalius.a: Andreas Vesalius was a Flemish anatomist and physician, renowned for his work in the field of human anatomy. He is best known for his groundbreaking book "De humani corporis fabrica," published in 1543, which laid the foundation for modern anatomy. Vesalius's meticulous dissections and detailed illustrations revolutionized the understanding of the human body during the Renaissance.
andreas-vesalius.o: Across all four renders, the style uses dense anatomical portraiture built from precise ink lines, crosshatching, and tightly controlled shading. Mostly monochrome black, white, and sepia tones, strong contrast, cropped profiles, and aged paper grounds give the illustrations the character of detailed anatomical plates.
