Crowded superhero figures are arranged in dramatic airborne or combat poses against angular city backgrounds, creating a forceful sense of motion and expressive anatomy.

mark-bradford.a: Mark Bradford is an American artist known for his large-scale abstract paintings that explore social and political themes. His work often incorporates materials found in urban environments, such as billboard paper and other detritus, to create textured and layered compositions that reflect the complexity of contemporary life.
mark-bradford.o: Across all four renders, the style is a dense, aggressively layered painting built from scraped impasto, broad directional strokes, drips, splatters, and collage-like fragments. Saturated reds, blacks, whites, and blues create a high-contrast field in which partial figures and architectural or diagrammatic forms emerge and dissolve into energetic abstraction.

mark-briscoe.a: Mark Briscoe is a professional wrestler known for his dynamic presence in the ring and his contributions to the world of wrestling.
mark-briscoe.o: The style combines heavily visible, directional paint strokes with crisp dark contour lines and densely worked surfaces. Saturated reds, blues, ochres, and deep greens create expressive, storybook scenes populated by animals, figures, and stylized landscapes, while repeated swirling marks give clouds, sky, foliage, and fur a tactile rhythm.

mark-brooks.a: Mark Brooks is a renowned comic book artist and illustrator known for his detailed and dynamic artwork, often associated with major comic publishers. His work is characterized by a strong sense of realism combined with fantastical elements, making him a prominent figure in the comic book industry.
mark-brooks.o: The style uses richly visible, layered brushwork to render dramatic female character portraits with intense gazes, dark costumes, and elaborate accessories. Warm ember tones against deep blacks and cool blue accents create a high-contrast, moody fantasy atmosphere, while fine painterly marks add both facial definition and ornate surface texture.

mark-catesby.a: Mark Catesby was an English naturalist and illustrator known for his pioneering work in documenting the flora and fauna of North America during the 18th century. His most notable work, "The Natural History of Carolina, Florida and the Bahama Islands," was the first published account of the natural history of North America, featuring detailed illustrations and descriptions of various species.
mark-catesby.o: The style combines highly detailed, finely rendered birds and botanical specimens with dense ornamental foliage and flowers. Restrained earthy greens, creams, reds, and pinks unify the compositions, while delicate linework and visible painted modeling give them the character of classic natural-history plates arranged as decorative panels.

mark-demsteader.a: Mark Demsteader is a contemporary British artist known for his evocative and expressive portraiture. His work often features detailed and moody representations of female figures, capturing emotional depth and introspection through his unique use of light and shadow.
mark-demsteader.o: The style combines subdued, moody portraiture with visible brushwork, sketch-like fine lines, and rough gestural marks that partially dissolve the figures into the background. Cropped faces, turned profiles, dark clothing, pale skin, and unruly hair create an introspective, melancholic mood, while the distorted poses and fragmented treatment add a subtly surreal quality.

mark-di-suvero.a: Mark di Suvero is an American abstract expressionist sculptor known for his monumental works made from industrial materials such as steel. Born in 1933, di Suvero's innovative approach to sculpture has made him a significant figure in contemporary art, particularly in the realm of public art installations.
mark-di-suvero.o: The style is highly realistic and photographically composed, presenting monumental industrial sculptures with crisp structural detail, strong perspective, and natural outdoor lighting. Saturated rust-orange and dark weathered metal stand out against expansive green landscapes and blue skies, with varied low-angle and contextual views giving the images a cinematic sense of scale.

mark-fiore.a: Mark Fiore is a renowned American political cartoonist known for his animated political cartoons. His work often features satirical and humorous takes on current events and social issues, earning him a Pulitzer Prize in 2010 for Editorial Cartooning.
mark-fiore.o: The style uses clean, graphic cartoon rendering with thick black contour lines, flat yet strongly varied color areas, and dense cross-scene detail. Exaggerated faces and expressive poses create a humorous, satirical ensemble of suited human caricatures and anthropomorphic animals in crowded jungle and courtroom-like settings.

mark-gertler.a: Mark Gertler was an influential British painter known for his distinctive style that combined elements of modernism and post-impressionism. Born in 1891, Gertler was part of the early 20th-century art scene in the United Kingdom, and his work often depicted intimate and reflective scenes. He was associated with the Bloomsbury Group and was known for his expressive portraits and still lifes.
mark-gertler.o: Across all four renders, the style uses carefully modelled painted faces, visible fine brushwork, and richly textured garments in a restrained palette dominated by reds, greens, browns, and black. Cropped groupings and individual bust portraits emphasize composed expressions, period clothing, and decorative surface detail with a polished illustrative clarity.

mark-grotjahn.a: Mark Grotjahn is an American artist known for his abstract and geometric paintings, often characterized by bold colors and intricate patterns. His work frequently explores themes of symmetry and optical illusion, drawing inspiration from both modernist and contemporary art movements.
mark-grotjahn.o: The style uses brightly colored geometric wedges radiating from central points, with strong bilateral or radial organization across every composition. Thick, visibly built-up paint and scraped, directional strokes give the flat graphic structures a tactile, handmade surface.

mark-hearld.a: Mark Hearld is a contemporary British artist known for his vibrant and imaginative works that draw inspiration from the natural world and British folklore. He is celebrated for his use of collage, printmaking, and mixed media, creating pieces that are both decorative and narrative in nature.
mark-hearld.o: The style combines visible, directional paint strokes with finely drawn outlines and selectively flat, graphic color shapes. Dense tropical birds, foliage, flowers, and patterned plumage fill the frame in an ornate, layered arrangement, using saturated reds, blues, creams, and dark accents for an energetic decorative effect.

mark-henson.a: Mark Henson is a contemporary American artist known for his visionary and psychedelic art. His work often explores themes of spirituality, consciousness, and the interconnectedness of life. Henson's paintings are celebrated for their vibrant colors, intricate details, and imaginative compositions that invite viewers into a world of fantasy and transcendence.
mark-henson.o: These landscapes combine richly visible brushwork with dense, finely articulated foliage, bark, clouds, and terrain. Saturated jewel-like colors, radiant internal light, winding paths, and impossible natural forms create an expansive dreamlike fantasy atmosphere across all four views.

mark-keathley.a: Mark Keathley is a contemporary American painter known for his serene and idyllic landscape paintings that often depict rural and natural settings. His works are characterized by a romantic realism that captures the beauty and tranquility of the American countryside, often featuring cabins, rivers, and lush forests.
mark-keathley.o: The style presents expansive, richly detailed wilderness scenes with visible painterly texture, saturated greens and warm golds, and strong atmospheric depth. Glowing low sunlight, mist, reflective water, seasonal foliage, and storybook rural details create a dreamy, grand romantic-fantasy mood across all four images.

mark-knight.a: Mark Knight is an illustrator known for his unique style that blends elements of fantasy and surrealism. His work often features intricate details and imaginative compositions, drawing inspiration from mythological and gothic themes. Knight's illustrations are characterized by their expressive and moody atmosphere, often exploring dark and whimsical subjects.
mark-knight.o: Across all four renders, the style uses dense illustrative tattoo imagery with heavy black outlines, intricate internal linework, and strongly expressive animal and humanoid forms. Saturated reds, oranges, pinks, and greens contrast against dark ink-heavy shading, producing ornate, dramatic compositions with a recurring grotesque and fantastical tone.

mark-kostabi.a: Mark Kostabi is an American artist known for his distinctive style that blends elements of surrealism and pop art. Born in 1960, Kostabi gained fame in the 1980s for his bold, colorful paintings that often feature faceless figures and urban themes. His work is characterized by a unique combination of abstraction and figurative elements, often exploring themes of identity and consumerism.
mark-kostabi.o: Across all four images, stylized figures and city settings are constructed from sharply faceted geometric planes, clean graphic contours, and strong blocks of saturated color. Deep shadows, bright highlights, and a fine printed grain create high contrast while preserving an illustrative, poster-like finish; recurring hats, checkerboard surfaces, and distorted proportions give the scenes a surreal character.

mark-lague.a: Mark Lague is a contemporary Canadian artist known for his impressionistic cityscapes and urban scenes. His work often captures the dynamic energy and atmosphere of bustling city life, using bold brushstrokes and vibrant colors to convey movement and light.
mark-lague.o: The style depicts dense urban street scenes with rain, traffic, reflective pavement, and towering buildings, rendered through visible broad brushwork and vertical scraped or streaked marks. Cool, subdued city tones are repeatedly punctuated by strong orange-red lights, with misty distance, luminous reflections, and high contrast creating an expressive, cinematic-feeling atmosphere without relying on photographic realism.

mark-manders.a: Mark Manders is a contemporary Dutch artist known for his sculptural installations that explore themes of identity and the human condition. His work often features fragmented and abstract forms, creating a sense of mystery and introspection.
mark-manders.o: The style presents monumental, fragmented human sculptures in bright gallery-like interiors, rendered with convincing weight, rough plaster texture, and abundant structural detail. Restrained beige and gray tones, stark architectural framing, and damaged classical-looking faces create an uncanny blend of realism, ruin, and surreal installation imagery.

mark-riddick.a: Mark Riddick is a renowned illustrator known for his intricate and dark artwork, often associated with the metal music scene. His work is characterized by detailed line work and a macabre aesthetic, frequently featuring themes of death and the supernatural.
mark-riddick.o: Across all four renders, the style uses dense monochrome fantasy illustration with fine engraved linework, intricate textures, and stark black-and-white contrast. Gothic figures, skulls, ravens, moons, barren landscapes, and monumental supernatural settings create a dark, epic visual language with heavily ornamented surfaces.

mark-rothko.a: Mark Rothko was an American painter known for his contributions to abstract expressionism, particularly through his color field paintings. Born in 1903 in Latvia, Rothko emigrated to the United States, where he developed his signature style characterized by large, luminous rectangles of color. His work is celebrated for its emotional depth and meditative qualities, often evoking a profound sense of introspection.
mark-rothko.o: Across all four renders, the style uses large geometric color fields arranged in a rigid grid, with recurring rectangular panels and strong horizontal and vertical divisions. Saturated reds and oranges are layered with deep near-black areas, while visible brush texture, softened transitions, and rough edges keep the geometry painterly rather than mechanically flat.

mark-ruwedel.a: Mark Ruwedel is an American photographer known for his exploration of landscapes and human impact on the environment. His work often focuses on the remnants of human activity in natural settings, capturing the intersection of nature and culture.
mark-ruwedel.o: Across all four renders, the style uses stark black-and-white photographic realism to depict isolated human-made forms in broad, arid landscapes. Strong tonal contrast, visible grain, spacious compositions, and carefully resolved weathered surfaces give the scenes a cinematic, quietly uncanny sense of monumental desolation.

mark-ryden.a: Mark Ryden is an American painter known for his distinctive style that blends pop culture with surrealism. His work often features a mix of whimsical and eerie elements, drawing on themes from childhood, fairy tales, and Victorian aesthetics. Ryden's paintings are characterized by their meticulous detail and dreamlike quality, often incorporating fantastical creatures and childlike figures.
mark-ryden.o: The style combines softly modeled, highly detailed portraiture with visible painterly texture, giving the figures a porcelain-doll quality and solid, sculptural presence. Subdued, earthy backgrounds and pastel garments support ornate clothing, floral decoration, woodland settings, and surreal child-animal pairings across the sheet.

mark-schultz.a: Mark Schultz is an American illustrator and comic book artist known for his work on series like "Xenozoic Tales." His style is characterized by detailed linework and a strong influence from classic adventure and fantasy art. Schultz's illustrations often feature dynamic compositions and heroic figures, drawing inspiration from the pulp magazines and comic books of the mid-20th century.
mark-schultz.o: The style combines monochrome, high-contrast fantasy illustration with visible ink lines, energetic brushwork, and dense textural detail in fur, clothing, rocks, and snow. Heroic human figures are paired with oversized or monstrous animals in dramatic wilderness scenes, giving the images an epic, rugged storybook quality.

mark-seliger.a: Mark Seliger is a renowned American photographer known for his iconic portraits of celebrities and musicians. His work has been featured in prominent publications such as Rolling Stone and Vanity Fair, showcasing his ability to capture the essence of his subjects with a unique blend of artistry and technical skill.
mark-seliger.o: Across all four renders, the style uses highly realistic, carefully detailed portrait photography with cinematic framing and strongly controlled lighting. It alternates monochrome and earthy, low-key color treatments, emphasizing expressive faces, distinctive clothing, seated poses, and a dark editorial mood.

mark-shaw.a: Mark Shaw was a renowned American photographer known for his work in fashion and celebrity photography during the mid-20th century. He gained fame for his elegant and sophisticated images, often capturing the glamour and style of the 1950s and 1960s. Shaw's work appeared in prominent publications such as Life magazine, and he was celebrated for his ability to portray the grace and charm of his subjects, including many iconic figures of the era.
mark-shaw.o: The style uses highly realistic, cinematic portrait photography with carefully staged period costumes, richly decorated interiors, and a restrained palette that shifts between monochrome, warm reds, and shadowed neutrals. Strong directional lighting, selective focus, motion blur, and ornate architectural detail create a polished, nostalgic fashion-editorial atmosphere.

mark-spain.a: Mark Spain is a contemporary artist known for his evocative and romantic figurative paintings. His work often features elegant and expressive portrayals of women, capturing moments of introspection and allure. Spain's art is characterized by a blend of classical and modern techniques, creating a unique style that resonates with a wide audience.
mark-spain.o: Across all four panels, the images use visible, broad, energetic paint strokes to model expressive figures, clothing, hair, and architectural interiors. Saturated reds stand out against deep brown-green surroundings and warm lamps, with dramatic cropping, lively poses, and densely populated dance scenes giving the style a theatrical, fashion-portrait character.

mark-steinmetz.a: Mark Steinmetz is an American photographer known for his black and white images that capture the subtle, everyday moments of life. His work often focuses on the youth and suburban settings of the United States, offering a reflective and intimate view of his subjects. Steinmetz's photography is celebrated for its ability to convey emotion and narrative through simple, yet powerful compositions.
mark-steinmetz.o: The style uses realistic black-and-white portrait photography with strong tonal contrast, candid direct gazes, and documentary-like moments staged within ordinary suburban surroundings. Shallow focus, occasional backlighting, natural textures, and loosely framed figures create an intimate, cinematic atmosphere across the four images.

mark-tobey.a: Mark Tobey is an American painter known for his contributions to abstract expressionism and his unique calligraphic style. Born in 1890, Tobey's work often reflects a synthesis of Eastern and Western artistic traditions, influenced by his interest in Zen Buddhism and Asian calligraphy. His art is characterized by intricate patterns and a focus on the spiritual and mystical aspects of life.
mark-tobey.o: Across all four renders, the style is an all-over abstract field built from dense, visibly layered paint marks and broad gestural strokes. Its mostly pale gray, white, and beige palette is repeatedly punctuated by rust, black, and occasional stronger pigment fragments, creating a heavily textured, energetic surface rather than recognizable subject matter.

mark-waid.a: Mark Waid is a renowned American comic book writer known for his work on titles such as "The Flash," "Kingdom Come," and "Daredevil." His storytelling is celebrated for its depth, character development, and innovative narratives that have significantly influenced the comic book industry.
mark-waid.o: Across all four renders, the style combines dense comic-book character imagery with visibly worked paint, broad directional strokes, heavy contouring, and strongly expressive faces and poses. Saturated reds, blues, greens, and oranges are pushed against deep shadows, creating high-energy scenes that feel dramatic, fantastical, and densely packed with action.

mark-wallinger.a: Mark Wallinger is a British artist known for his diverse and thought-provoking works that often explore themes of identity, politics, and perception. His art spans various mediums, including sculpture, painting, and video, and he has been recognized for his ability to engage with contemporary social issues through a conceptual lens.
mark-wallinger.o: The style presents highly realistic, meticulously detailed museum interiors populated by monumental sculptural installations and small human figures for scale. Restrained neutral tones, polished surfaces, strong architectural framing, and selective glowing or dramatic lighting create a dark, contemplative gallery atmosphere.

marker-drawing.a: Marker drawing is a technique that involves using markers to create vibrant and detailed illustrations. It is known for its bold colors and ability to produce both fine lines and broad strokes, making it a versatile medium for artists.
marker-drawing.o: Across all four renders, the style combines expressive portrait drawing with forceful black contouring, vivid graphic color blocks, and selectively rough marker or ink textures. Faces and creatures are pushed toward surreal exaggeration, balancing recognizable features with flat, high-contrast shapes and loose gestural marks.

marko-manev.a: Marko Manev is a contemporary artist known for his work in graphic design and illustration. His art often explores themes of surrealism and fantasy, creating immersive and atmospheric visuals that captivate audiences.
marko-manev.o: Across all four renders, stark monochrome landscapes place tiny silhouetted figures against immense cliffs, skies, and glowing banks of mist. Extreme backlighting, deep blacks, scattered stars, and broad empty space create a dark, surreal, monumental atmosphere.

marlene-dumas.a: Marlene Dumas is a South African-born contemporary artist known for her evocative and emotionally charged paintings. Her work often explores themes of identity, sexuality, and the human condition, using a distinctive style characterized by expressive brushwork and a muted color palette. Dumas's paintings are celebrated for their psychological depth and ability to convey complex emotions.
marlene-dumas.o: Across all four images, the style uses close-up portrait faces rendered with visibly loose, layered brushwork and delicate drawn marks. Muted flesh, blue-gray, pink, and brown washes create an austere, unsettling mood, while distorted features and heavy eye treatment make the expressions feel raw and psychologically intense.

marquetry.a: Marquetry is a decorative art form that involves applying pieces of veneer to a structure to form intricate patterns and designs. Originating in the 16th century, it became popular in Europe for embellishing furniture and decorative objects. The technique requires precision and skill, often using woods of different colors to create detailed images and patterns.
marquetry.o: Across the sheet, richly layered woodgrain-like marks model floral motifs, landscapes, portraiture, and geometric ornament in a unified sepia range. Fine drawn contours, dense surface detail, strong dark-light separation, and carved-looking decorative patterning give the images an ornate, handcrafted illustrative character.

marsden-hartley.a: Marsden Hartley was an American modernist painter known for his bold use of color and expressive forms. Born in 1877, Hartley was a prominent figure in the early 20th-century art scene, often exploring themes of spirituality and identity through his work. His style is characterized by vibrant colors, abstract forms, and a unique blend of symbolism and expressionism, making him a key figure in American modernism.
marsden-hartley.o: The style uses vivid primary-like colors, heavy black contours, angular geometric shapes, and flattened areas of paint to create forceful abstract figures and objects. Visible brush marks and rough, built-up canvas texture keep the graphic compositions painterly, while repeated eyes, rays, stripes, and ornamental motifs give them an expressive surreal quality.

marsel-van-oosten.a: Marsel van Oosten is a renowned wildlife photographer known for his striking images of nature and animals. His work often captures the beauty and complexity of the natural world, earning him numerous awards and recognition in the field of photography.
marsel-van-oosten.o: Across all four renders, the style is cinematic and highly realistic, combining finely resolved animal subjects or distant birds with vast, sculptural landscapes. Subdued blue-gray and brown palettes are shaped by strong golden backlighting, deep shadows, atmospheric haze, selective focus, and expansive, dreamlike compositions.

marta-abad-blay.a: Marta Abad Blay is a contemporary artist known for her vibrant and whimsical illustrations that often feature floral and nature elements. Her work is characterized by a playful and imaginative style that captures the essence of youth and fantasy, making her a notable figure in modern illustration.
marta-abad-blay.o: The style combines vividly colored illustrative figures and animals with visible painterly brushwork, fine drawn contours, and selectively flat color. Dense tropical foliage, flowers, houseplants, geometric furnishings, and patterned surfaces create richly packed decorative compositions across both portrait and interior scenes.

marta-bevacqua.a: Marta Bevacqua is a contemporary photographer known for her ethereal and dreamlike imagery. Her work often explores themes of femininity and nature, capturing moments of serene beauty and delicate emotion. Bevacqua's photography is characterized by its soft focus, natural lighting, and detailed compositions, creating a sense of intimacy and whimsy.
marta-bevacqua.o: The style uses intimate, highly realistic close-up portrait photography with natural skin texture, freckles, wet hair, and emotionally direct expressions. Subdued teal-green and earthy tones, cinematic framing, shallow focus, reflective water, and foreground foliage create a moody, tactile atmosphere across all four images.

martha-rosler.a: Martha Rosler is an influential American artist known for her work in photography, video, and performance art. She gained prominence in the 1970s with her politically charged and socially conscious pieces that often critique consumer culture, war, and the role of women in society. Rosler's work is characterized by its incisive commentary and innovative use of media, making her a significant figure in contemporary art.
martha-rosler.o: The style combines richly detailed, photographic-looking landscapes and decayed architectural settings with an aged, grainy print texture, subdued warm colors, and strong retro coloration. Surreal juxtapositions⁠—brightly dressed figures, obsolete objects, ruined spaces, and vast natural vistas⁠—are assembled with a tactile collage sensibility and an unsettling, dreamlike mood.

martin-ansin.a: Martin Ansin is a contemporary illustrator known for his detailed and dynamic artwork, often featured in movie posters and pop culture illustrations. His work is recognized for its intricate line work and vibrant color palettes, capturing the essence of cinematic and comic book aesthetics.
martin-ansin.o: Across all four renders, expressive portraits and character groupings are built from visible directional paint strokes, angular fine linework, and densely layered forms. Saturated reds, oranges, deep blues, and teal-greens create a high-contrast illustrated-painterly look, with dramatic cropping and overlapping figures giving the compositions poster-like energy.

martin-creed.a: Martin Creed is a British artist known for his innovative and often minimalist approach to art. He gained prominence as part of the Young British Artists movement in the 1990s and is celebrated for his conceptual works that challenge traditional notions of art. Creed's work spans various mediums, including sculpture, painting, and performance, often characterized by a playful and thought-provoking nature.
martin-creed.o: The style presents vivid, cleanly separated bands of saturated color within realistic contemporary gallery interiors. Strong perspective, repeated geometric stripes, spacious white architecture, and crisp flat surfaces create a bold, polished installation-like look across the four renders.

martin-deschambault.a: Martin Deschambault is a contemporary artist known for his work in the field of concept art and illustration, particularly within the science fiction genre. His art often explores futuristic themes and imaginative worlds, showcasing a blend of detailed environments and dynamic compositions.
martin-deschambault.o: Across all four renders, broad visible brushwork, layered texture, and energetic strokes give the landscapes a richly painterly, expressive finish. Monumental cliffs, castles, forests, and distant cities are staged as cinematic fantasy scenes, using saturated blues, greens, and orange light to emphasize scale, atmosphere, and adventure.

martin-grelle.a: Martin Grelle is an American painter known for his vivid depictions of Native American life and the American West. His work often features detailed portrayals of indigenous peoples, landscapes, and historical scenes, capturing the spirit and culture of the frontier era.
martin-grelle.o: Across all four renders, broad mountain vistas and travelling horse riders are painted with visible, energetic strokes and finely varied surface texture. Saturated blue skies, green valleys, white snow, and warm costume accents create an expansive, heroic wilderness mood with strong atmospheric depth.

martin-johnson-heade.a: Martin Johnson Heade was an American painter known for his landscapes, seascapes, and depictions of tropical birds and flowers. Active in the 19th century, Heade was associated with the Hudson River School and is celebrated for his detailed and atmospheric works that often blend realism with romanticism.
martin-johnson-heade.o: Across all four renders, richly layered flowers and wetland vegetation are integrated with expansive, cloud-heavy landscapes in a romantic, dreamlike composition. Visible brush texture, softly blended atmospheric distance, deep greens, dusky skies, and luminous pink and white blossoms create a painterly yet highly detailed look.

martin-kippenberger.a: Martin Kippenberger is a German artist known for his diverse and provocative body of work, which spans painting, sculpture, installation, and performance art. He was a key figure in the Neo-Expressionist movement and is recognized for his critical and often humorous take on contemporary culture and art itself. Kippenberger's work frequently challenges traditional artistic conventions and explores themes of identity, politics, and society.
martin-kippenberger.o: Across all four renders, the style combines dense, visibly worked paint with angular, fragmented compositions and strong saturated reds, greens, blues, and pinks. Figures and interior situations remain recognizable but are distorted into theatrical, surreal tableaux, with broad strokes, fine linear marks, drips, and layered collage-like planes contributing to an expressive studio-painting surface.

martin-lewis.a: Martin Lewis is an Australian-born American artist known for his mastery in printmaking, particularly etching and drypoint. He gained recognition for his detailed and atmospheric depictions of urban life in New York City during the early 20th century. Lewis's work is characterized by its strong use of light and shadow, creating a sense of depth and mood that captures the essence of city life.
martin-lewis.o: The style is monochrome and strongly cinematic, using deep blacks, brilliant lamp and moon highlights, reflective wet streets, and atmospheric rain or fog. Recurring silhouettes, period urban architecture, bridges, vehicles, ships, and pedestrians create a moody retro city narrative with dramatic backlighting and luminous haze.

martin-margiela.a: Martin Margiela is a Belgian fashion designer known for his avant-garde and deconstructivist approach to fashion. He founded the fashion house Maison Martin Margiela, which became renowned for its innovative and unconventional designs that challenged traditional fashion norms. Margiela's work often features deconstruction, anonymity, and a focus on the conceptual aspects of clothing, making him a pivotal figure in contemporary fashion.
martin-margiela.o: The style combines restrained studio photography with sculptural, deconstructed fashion: raw, frayed textiles and transparent plastic conceal or reshape the human body. Muted off-white and gray tones, tactile material detail, cropped portraits, and an uncanny surreal mood unify the four renders.

martin-parr.a: Martin Parr is a renowned British photographer known for his satirical and humorous approach to documentary photography. His work often explores themes of consumerism, leisure, and social norms, capturing the quirks and idiosyncrasies of everyday life. Parr's photographs are characterized by their vibrant colors, candid compositions, and a keen eye for detail, making ordinary scenes appear extraordinary.
martin-parr.o: The style uses realistic, cinematic street photography with carefully composed, characterful figures in urban and seaside settings. Restrained vintage color, period clothing, oversized sunglasses, classic vehicles, and crisp environmental detail create a playful retro fashion-documentary atmosphere.

martin-puryear.a: Martin Puryear is an American sculptor known for his devotion to traditional craft techniques and his exploration of form and material. His work often reflects a deep understanding of woodworking and a commitment to creating pieces that resonate with cultural and historical references, particularly those related to African American heritage.
martin-puryear.o: The style presents large sculptural forms woven from natural reeds or rattan, emphasizing open latticework, repeated linear patterns, and sweeping organic curves. Subdued earth tones, clean gallery interiors, controlled lighting, and carefully staged views give the renders a polished illustrative and exhibition-documentation character.

martin-rak.a: Martin Rak is a contemporary photographer known for his captivating landscape photography, often capturing the serene and mystical beauty of nature. His work is characterized by an ethereal quality, focusing on the interplay of light and shadow in natural settings.
martin-rak.o: The style uses monochrome, realistic landscape photography with strong tonal separation, deep shadows, and luminous pale fog. Rolling farmland, isolated trees, distant ridges, and occasional paths are arranged as atmospheric cinematic vistas, with mist creating layered depth and a quiet, moody sense of scale.

martin-rowson.a: Martin Rowson is a British cartoonist and illustrator known for his sharp political satire and distinctive caricature style. His work often appears in major newspapers and magazines, where he uses humor and exaggeration to critique political figures and societal issues.
martin-rowson.o: Across all four renders, the style combines dense, hand-painted brush texture with energetic black contour drawing, vivid color, and strongly exaggerated anatomy. Crowded scenes of grotesque human, animal, and hybrid characters use theatrical expressions, dark tonal contrast, and fantastical surreal imagery.

martin-schoeller.a: Martin Schoeller is a renowned German photographer known for his distinctive close-up portraits that capture the essence of his subjects with striking clarity and detail. His work often features celebrities and everyday people alike, presented in a way that emphasizes the individuality and humanity of each person. Schoeller's style is characterized by its hyper-realistic approach, often using high-resolution techniques to bring out the intricate details of the human face.
martin-schoeller.o: This style presents highly realistic, tightly framed character portraits with exceptionally legible skin texture, wrinkles, pores, hair, and facial hair. Soft neutral lighting and pale backgrounds keep attention on direct gazes and individualized features, while shallow focus gently separates the faces from their surroundings.

martin-schongauer.a: Martin Schongauer was a German engraver and painter from the 15th century, known for his detailed and intricate engravings. His work is characterized by fine lines and a high level of detail, often depicting religious and mythological themes. Schongauer's engravings were influential in the development of printmaking in Europe and inspired later artists such as Albrecht Dürer.
martin-schongauer.o: The style uses highly detailed monochrome ink drawing on a warm, antique paper ground, with delicate contour lines, dense hatching, and crosshatching shaping faces, fabric, animals, and architecture. It combines classical-looking portrait studies and elaborate fantastical scenes with grotesque composite figures, ornamental details, and surreal visual juxtapositions.

martin-scorsese.a: Martin Scorsese is an acclaimed American filmmaker known for his influential contributions to cinema, particularly in the genres of crime and drama. His works often explore themes of identity, guilt, and redemption, and are characterized by their innovative use of camera techniques and storytelling. Scorsese has directed numerous iconic films, including "Taxi Driver," "Goodfellas," and "The Departed," earning him a place among the most respected directors in the history of film.
martin-scorsese.o: The style uses richly textured, visible brushwork to render stern, highly detailed character portraits with strong facial modeling and dramatic shadow. Saturated red, black, cream, and deep blue dominate the palette, while tight crops, formal poses, and graphic background blocks give the images a bold editorial presence.

martin-stranka.a: Martin Stranka is a contemporary photographer known for his surreal and dreamlike imagery. His work often explores themes of solitude and introspection, blending reality with fantasy to create ethereal and thought-provoking compositions.
martin-stranka.o: The style is cinematic and realistic, using muted teal-and-sepia grading, strong backlighting, deep silhouettes, and broad expanses of empty sky or roadway. Solitary figures and transforming debris recur in atmospheric, surreal scenes shaped by mist, motion, and a dark dreamlike mood.

martin-whatson.a: Martin Whatson is a contemporary Norwegian street artist known for his vibrant and dynamic graffiti art. His work often combines traditional street art techniques with modern themes, creating pieces that are both visually striking and thought-provoking. Whatson's art is characterized by its use of stencils and spray paint, often featuring urban landscapes and cultural references.
martin-whatson.o: Across all four renders, recognizable hooded human figures are rendered in largely monochrome, heavily shaded forms and surrounded by explosive saturated paint. Broad visible brushwork, sharp dark outlines, drips, splatters, and graffiti-like marks create an energetic mixed-media mural effect against gray grounds.

martin-wittfooth.a: Martin Wittfooth is a contemporary artist known for his surreal and fantastical paintings that often explore themes of nature and the human condition. His work frequently features animals in dreamlike settings, combining rich symbolism with intricate detail.
martin-wittfooth.o: These images use richly visible, broad painterly strokes to build highly detailed animal forms, tangled vegetation, and reflective wetland settings. Muted blue-green shadows contrast with warm orange fire and autumnal accents, creating expressive, fantastical scenes in which hybrid animals and elemental flames feel dreamlike yet tangible.

martina-hoogland-ivanow.a: Martina Hoogland Ivanow is a Swedish photographer known for her evocative and atmospheric imagery. Her work often explores themes of isolation, nature, and the human condition, capturing a sense of mystery and introspection. Ivanow's photography is celebrated for its unique blend of dreamlike qualities and a painterly approach, making her a distinctive voice in contemporary photography.
martina-hoogland-ivanow.o: The style uses realistic, cinematic portrait photography with intimate framing, selective focus, and strongly controlled light. Muted teal, brown, and amber tones, deep shadows, tactile fabrics, aged interiors, and emotionally charged gestures create a dark, theatrical atmosphere across the four images.

martine-franck.a: Martine Franck is a renowned Belgian-born photographer known for her work in documentary and humanist photography. She was a member of the prestigious Magnum Photos agency and was celebrated for her ability to capture the essence of the human condition through her lens. Her work often focused on themes of solitude, introspection, and the everyday lives of people, with a particular emphasis on European settings.
martine-franck.o: The style uses stark black-and-white photographic imagery with strong tonal separation, deep shadows, and sharply directional light. It combines intimate portraits and solitary figures with atmospheric environmental scenes, often using selective focus, grain, and cinematic framing to create a melancholic, observational mood.

martine-johanna.a: Martine Johanna is a contemporary Dutch artist known for her vibrant and emotive portraits that often explore themes of femininity and introspection. Her work is characterized by a blend of realism and surrealism, capturing the delicate balance between the real and the imagined.
martine-johanna.o: The style combines highly detailed, painterly close-up portraits with delicate visible linework and fine, layered brushstrokes. Saturated coral, turquoise, pink, cream, and blue hues unify the expressive faces, floral framing, patterned fabrics, and tightly cropped fashion-editorial compositions.

martiros-saryan.a: Martiros Saryan was an Armenian painter known for his vibrant and expressive works that often depicted the landscapes and culture of Armenia. Born in 1880, Saryan became a prominent figure in Armenian art, blending elements of modernism and symbolism to create a unique visual language that celebrated the natural beauty and folklore of his homeland.
martiros-saryan.o: Across the four renders, the style combines strongly angular, fashion-oriented portraiture with a landscape scene, using saturated reds, blues, oranges, and deep shadows. Visible directional brushwork and textured paint surfaces coexist with clean graphic shapes, dark contouring, and tightly cropped, expressive compositions.

martyn-turner.a: Martyn Turner is a renowned cartoonist and illustrator known for his satirical and political works. His illustrations often feature bold lines and a distinctive style that captures the essence of the subjects he portrays. Turner has contributed to various publications, making a significant impact in the world of editorial cartoons.
martyn-turner.o: The style uses monochrome ink drawing with energetic fine contour lines, dense crosshatching, and occasional broad wash-like black areas. High contrast, stark white space, exaggerated figures, and richly described ruined or theatrical environments create an expressive, surreal graphic-narrative mood across the set.

marvel.a: Marvel is a globally recognized entertainment company known for its iconic comic book characters and expansive cinematic universe. Founded in 1939, Marvel has become a cornerstone of pop culture, creating beloved superheroes like Spider-Man, Iron Man, and Captain America, and producing blockbuster films and series.
marvel.o: The style combines densely layered comic-book character imagery with visible painterly brushwork, sharp fine detailing, and strong graphic contours. Saturated reds, blues, golds, and greens are pushed against deep shadows, while energetic poses, explosive effects, and tightly packed faces create an expressive, high-impact superhero montage.

mary-anning.a: Mary Anning was a pioneering English fossil collector and paleontologist in the early 19th century. She made significant contributions to the understanding of prehistoric life, discovering several important fossils along the Jurassic Coast of England. Her work laid foundational stones for the field of paleontology, despite facing challenges due to her gender and social status.
mary-anning.o: These images use richly textured, visible brushwork to render realistic women, seabirds, clothing, rocks, and ocean settings with carefully observed detail. The subdued, earthy palette and weathered surface texture create a solemn, classical coastal atmosphere, while portrait-like figures anchor each composition.

mary-blair.a: Mary Blair is a renowned American artist and illustrator known for her work with The Walt Disney Company. She played a significant role in the visual development of classic films such as "Cinderella," "Alice in Wonderland," and "Peter Pan." Blair's distinct style, characterized by vibrant colors and imaginative designs, has left a lasting impact on animation and children's literature.
mary-blair.o: Across all four renders, richly textured brushwork combines with bold outlines, geometric shapes, and strongly saturated colors. Dense floral and animal motifs, theatrical figures, dark grounds, and decorative framing create an ornate, expressive storybook world with a dreamy fairytale atmosphere.

mary-bradish-titcomb.a: Mary Bradish Titcomb was an American painter known for her impressionistic style, often focusing on portraits and landscapes. Born in 1858, she was part of the Boston School and contributed significantly to American art during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
mary-bradish-titcomb.o: The style is built from visible, directional oil-paint strokes, with layered impasto and expressive, loosely resolved forms. Garden scenes and elegantly dressed figures emerge from dark foliage and abundant flowers through subdued earthy colors, warm highlights, and richly textured brushwork.

mary-cassatt.a: Mary Cassatt was an American painter and printmaker, known for her work in the Impressionist movement. Born in 1844, she spent much of her adult life in France, where she became friends with Edgar Degas and exhibited with the Impressionists. Cassatt is celebrated for her portrayals of the intimate bonds between mothers and children, capturing the tenderness and warmth of domestic life.
mary-cassatt.o: Across all four images, softly modeled family portraits are built from visible oil-paint strokes, layered color, and richly textured surfaces. Cropped embraces, sleeping children, pastel garments, and expressive faces create an intimate, tender mood, with subdued blue, pink, cream, and warm earth tones throughout.

mary-charles.a: Mary Charles is a fictional representation inspired by a blend of artistic styles, often associated with folk and naïve art traditions. Her work is characterized by a whimsical and enchanting portrayal of nature, often integrating elements of fantasy and surrealism. The style reflects a deep connection to rural and pastoral themes, celebrating the beauty and simplicity of the natural world.
mary-charles.o: The style combines illustrative, finely painted forms with visible brush texture, dense botanical detail, and richly layered ornamental surfaces. Saturated autumnal and floral colors unify portraits, village landscapes, gardens, and nocturnal scenes into a lush, storybook-like visual world.

mary-delany.a: Mary Delany was an 18th-century English artist known for her exquisite botanical collages. She is celebrated for creating intricate paper mosaics that depict flowers with remarkable detail and accuracy, blending art with scientific observation.
mary-delany.o: Across all four renders, flowers and foliage are rendered with visible fine brushwork, layered texture, and carefully observed botanical detail against a nearly black ground. The restrained dark palette is punctuated by saturated reds, pinks, oranges, and whites, with strong light-dark separation and densely arranged ornamental plant forms.

mary-ellen-mark.a: Mary Ellen Mark is a renowned American photographer known for her photojournalistic and documentary work. Her career spanned several decades, during which she captured powerful images of marginalized communities and individuals, often focusing on social issues and human experiences. Her work is characterized by its empathetic approach and ability to tell compelling stories through the lens of her camera.
mary-ellen-mark.o: The style uses stark black-and-white photography with strong tonal contrast, intimate portrait framing, and selective focus. Its candid domestic settings, solemn expressions, vintage clothing, and richly textured interiors create a dark, psychologically charged documentary-like atmosphere across the four images.

mary-engelbreit.a: Mary Engelbreit is an American illustrator known for her distinctive and charming artwork, often featured in children's books, greeting cards, and home decor. Her work is characterized by a whimsical and nostalgic style, drawing inspiration from folk art and storybook illustrations, and is widely recognized for its intricate details and vivid color palettes.
mary-engelbreit.o: The style combines visible hand-painted texture with crisp illustrative outlines, densely layering vivid colors, floral motifs, ceramics, textiles, furniture, and patterned surfaces. Storybook characters and animals appear within highly decorative domestic and garden settings, with ornate details and strong geometric accents such as checkerboards and framed panels.

mary-fedden.a: Mary Fedden is a renowned British artist known for her distinctive still life and landscape paintings. Born in 1915, she studied at the Slade School of Fine Art and later became a prominent figure in the British art scene. Her work is celebrated for its whimsical charm, bold use of color, and playful compositions, often depicting domestic and rural scenes with a unique modernist flair.
mary-fedden.o: These interiors combine visible, varied brushwork with graphic outlines, flat color blocks, and strongly patterned surfaces. Saturated reds, pinks, blues, and greens organize densely arranged still lifes of flowers, plants, ceramics, furniture, and domestic animals, with geometric backdrops and ornamental fabrics adding visual rhythm.

mary-heilmann.a: Mary Heilmann is an American artist known for her vibrant abstract paintings that blend elements of minimalism and pop culture. Her work often explores the interplay of color and form, creating dynamic compositions that challenge traditional artistic boundaries. Heilmann's unique approach has made her a significant figure in contemporary art, influencing a generation of artists with her bold use of color and innovative techniques.
mary-heilmann.o: Across all four works, vivid geometric color fields dominate, arranged as angular blocks, triangles, and rectangles rather than recognizable subjects. The surfaces visibly retain broad brushwork and thick, uneven paint, combining hard-edged composition with a tactile handmade finish.

mary-jane-ansell.a: Mary Jane Ansell is a contemporary British painter known for her detailed and ethereal portraits that blend classical techniques with modern sensibilities. Her work often features serene and introspective female subjects, capturing a timeless elegance and youthful innocence.
mary-jane-ansell.o: The style uses highly realistic, finely resolved portraiture with softly modeled faces, individual hair strands, fabric folds, and delicate floral or butterfly details. Restrained cream, black, brown, and muted red tones stand out against dark studio grounds, with strong tonal separation and carefully composed fashion-editorial framing.

mary-katrantzou.a: Mary Katrantzou is a Greek fashion designer known for her innovative use of digital prints and bold, colorful designs. She gained prominence in the fashion world for her unique approach to textile design, often incorporating intricate patterns and vibrant colors into her collections. Katrantzou's work is celebrated for its creativity and ability to transform traditional fashion elements into modern, avant-garde pieces.
mary-katrantzou.o: The style combines polished fashion-editorial realism with densely patterned, ornamental garments and dramatic sculptural silhouettes. Botanical and architectural imagery is layered across the clothing in vivid blues, oranges, greens, and creams, while the sheet alternates clean runway-style photography with fine-lined fashion-illustration treatments.

mary-quant.a: Mary Quant is a renowned British fashion designer credited with popularizing the miniskirt and hot pants in the 1960s. She played a pivotal role in the mod and youth fashion movements, bringing bold and playful designs to the forefront of British culture. Her work is characterized by its vibrant colors, geometric patterns, and innovative use of materials, making her a key figure in the Swinging Sixties.
mary-quant.o: The style combines polished fashion portraiture with simplified graphic illustration, uniting realistic faces and hair with flat, sharply separated color fields. Saturated orange, pink, green, yellow, and black create a bold retro look, reinforced by geometric bob hairstyles, oversized patterns, stylized clothing, and repeated editorial poses.

mary-sibande.a: Mary Sibande is a South African artist known for her work exploring themes of identity, race, and gender through sculpture and photography. Her art often features a fictional character, Sophie, who represents the complexities of post-apartheid South Africa. Sibande's work is recognized for its vivid use of color and intricate detailing, often incorporating elements of fashion and historical references.
mary-sibande.o: The style presents surreal haute-couture figures in highly elaborate, sculptural garments, with enormous ruffles, folded fabric, floral forms, and theatrical headwear. Strong monochromatic color treatments⁠—especially saturated blue, alongside a white variation⁠—combine with expansive skies, fields, and dramatic editorial posing to create a dreamy, cinematic fashion-image aesthetic.

masaaki-sasamoto.a: Masaaki Sasamoto is a contemporary artist known for his intricate and ethereal digital paintings that often blend elements of fantasy and surrealism. His work is characterized by a delicate balance between the fantastical and the realistic, often exploring themes of nature and human connection.
masaaki-sasamoto.o: The style combines finely rendered, painterly portraiture with dense botanical ornament, embroidered textiles, and antique-looking surface texture. Muted olive, cream, brown, and black tones are punctuated by gold-like accents and deep shadows, while close cropping and delicate faces create a dreamy, decorative atmosphere.

masaaki-yuasa.a: Masaaki Yuasa is a renowned Japanese animator and director known for his unique and imaginative style. He has worked on a variety of projects, including films and television series, that often explore surreal and fantastical themes. Yuasa's work is characterized by its fluid animation, bold visual choices, and a distinctive blend of humor and emotion.
masaaki-yuasa.o: Across all four renders, the style uses vivid flat color, strong dark contouring, and densely packed illustrative detail. It combines dynamic anime-like characters and vehicles with surreal, fantastical environments, exaggerated perspective, and crowded dreamlike landscapes.

masaccio.a: Masaccio was an influential Italian painter of the early Renaissance , known for his pioneering use of perspective and chiaroscuro. Born in 1401, he played a crucial role in the development of naturalism in art, creating works that emphasized realistic human figures and spatial depth. His frescoes, particularly those in the Brancacci Chapel, are celebrated for their innovative approach to composition and light.
masaccio.o: The style uses highly detailed, realistic painted figures with carefully modelled faces, individualized expressions, and visible fine brushwork. Restrained reds, ochres, browns, blues, and greens unify crowded historical group compositions, while worn architectural surfaces and textured paint give the images an aged, material presence.

masahisa-fukase.a: Masahisa Fukase was a renowned Japanese photographer known for his deeply personal and often haunting imagery. His work frequently explored themes of isolation, identity, and the passage of time, often using stark black and white photography to convey a sense of melancholy and introspection. Fukase's most famous series, "The Solitude of Ravens," is celebrated for its powerful emotional impact and innovative use of photographic techniques.
masahisa-fukase.o: Across all four images, the style uses stark black-and-white portrait photography with deep blacks, bright highlights, and visibly grainy texture. Close cropping, obscured faces, expressive poses, and hard directional or backlighting create an intimate, cinematic atmosphere of tension and introspection.

masami-teraoka.a: Masami Teraoka is a Japanese-American contemporary artist known for his work that blends traditional Japanese ukiyo-e styles with modern themes. Born in 1936 in Japan, Teraoka's art often explores cultural and social issues, using a unique fusion of Eastern and Western artistic techniques.
masami-teraoka.o: The style combines finely drawn, highly ornamental figures with densely patterned garments, flowers, animals, and swirling natural forms. Saturated reds, blues, creams, and dark neutrals are bounded by delicate lines, while waves, hair, fabric, and foliage create continuous flowing motion across the compositions.

masamune-shirow.a: Masamune Shirow is a renowned Japanese manga artist and writer, best known for his influential works in the cyberpunk genre, including 'Ghost in the Shell' and 'Appleseed.' His art is characterized by its intricate detail, futuristic themes, and a blend of technology with human elements, often exploring philosophical and existential themes.
masamune-shirow.o: The style uses densely packed, highly detailed character scenes rendered as expressive graphic illustrations, with fine ink-like outlines, crisp descriptive edges, and selectively modeled color. Saturated oranges, reds, blues, and skin tones stand out against dark mechanical clutter, creating a vivid, high-contrast science-fiction tableau with surreal combinations of humans, machines, and debris.

masao-yamamoto.a: Masao Yamamoto is a Japanese photographer known for his small-scale, intimate photographs that explore themes of memory, nature, and the passage of time. His work often features a delicate interplay of light and shadow, capturing fleeting moments with a sense of tranquility and introspection.
masao-yamamoto.o: Across all four renders, the style uses restrained near-monochrome tones, heavy silhouettes, deep shadows, and broad areas of atmospheric emptiness. Grain, fog, soft horizons, and isolated natural or human forms create a quiet, ominous, dreamlike cinematic mood.

mass-effect.a: Mass Effect is a popular science fiction video game series developed by BioWare, known for its rich storytelling, complex characters, and expansive universe. Set in a future where humanity has discovered interstellar travel, the series explores themes of exploration, conflict, and diplomacy across the galaxy.
mass-effect.o: Across all four renders, the style combines visibly brushed, scraped paint with fine graphic linework and richly layered character details. Strong red-and-blue color contrasts, deep shadows, luminous edge lighting, and tightly framed heroic portraits create an intense science-fiction character-poster look.

massimiliano-fuksas.a: Massimiliano Fuksas is an Italian architect known for his innovative and bold architectural designs. His work often features futuristic and organic forms, pushing the boundaries of modern architecture with a focus on fluidity and dynamic structures.
massimiliano-fuksas.o: The style presents photorealistic, cinematic architectural visions built from immense sculptural forms, translucent membranes, glass, and branching organic frameworks. Carefully composed urban and interior scenes use daylight, warm interior glow, dramatic scale, and intricate geometric structures to create a futuristic yet plausible atmosphere.

massimo-vignelli.a: Massimo Vignelli was an influential Italian designer known for his work in graphic design, furniture, and interior design. He was a proponent of modernist design principles and believed in the power of simplicity and clarity in design. Vignelli's work is characterized by its use of geometric forms, bold typography, and a limited color palette, often employing black, white, and red.
massimo-vignelli.o: The style combines realistic urban photography and portraiture with bold, hard-edged geometric graphics in saturated red, blue, black, and cream. Flat color fields, oversized circles and angular bands, tiled architectural settings, and a subtle grain unify the varied compositions into a graphic editorial look.

massimo-vitali.a: Massimo Vitali is an Italian photographer known for his large-scale images of beaches and public spaces, capturing the essence of leisure and social interaction. His work often explores themes of mass tourism and the human presence within natural landscapes, using a distinctive high vantage point to create expansive, detailed scenes.
massimo-vitali.o: Across all four renders, the style is photographic and highly realistic, with expansive coastal compositions, crisp natural textures, and saturated turquoise water against pale rock and blue sky. Crowds of bathers and rolling surf provide recurring human scale and motion, while atmospheric sea haze and broad cinematic framing soften the distant horizon.

massive-scale.a: Massive scale is a concept often associated with grand, monumental structures or ideas that evoke a sense of awe due to their sheer size or complexity. In various fields, it can refer to anything from large-scale architectural projects to expansive narrative worlds in literature and film.
massive-scale.o: The style uses highly realistic, cinematic landscape rendering to make immense mountains, cliffs, waves, and celestial bodies dwarf tiny human figures. Subdued blue-gray and earthy tones, strong light-dark separation, atmospheric mist, and sweeping forms create an epic sense of scale with surreal science-fiction worldbuilding.

mat-collishaw.a: Mat Collishaw is a contemporary British artist known for his provocative and visually striking works that often explore themes of beauty, desire, and decay. His art frequently incorporates elements of photography, sculpture, and digital media, creating immersive and thought-provoking experiences.
mat-collishaw.o: The style presents richly layered floral still lifes against near-black grounds, using intense highlights and deep shadows to make petals, glass, water, and stems feel tactile and dimensional. Dense, ornate arrangements are balanced by large areas of negative space, while delicate brushwork and expressive, slightly surreal compositions give the bouquets a dramatic, theatrical presence.

mathew-brady.a: Mathew Brady was a pioneering American photographer known for his documentation of the American Civil War and his portraits of prominent figures of the 19th century. His work is considered foundational in the field of photojournalism, capturing the stark realities of war and the personalities of his time with a meticulous eye for detail and composition.
mathew-brady.o: Across all four renders, the style presents highly realistic black-and-white period portraits staged in an outdoor camp setting, with crisp faces and clothing against softly blurred backgrounds. Strong tonal contrast, visible photographic grain, formal poses, and selective focus give the images a cinematic archival-photograph character.

mati-klarwein.a: Mati Klarwein is known for his visionary and surreal artwork, often blending cultural and spiritual themes. His work is characterized by intricate details, vibrant colors, and a fusion of various cultural influences, reflecting his diverse background and experiences.
mati-klarwein.o: The style combines densely layered painted imagery with intricate fine linework, ornamental framing, and highly saturated reds, blues, and golds. Monumental eyes, faces, animals, rivers, cities, and landscapes are arranged in dramatic symmetrical or radial compositions, with strong contrast and surreal spatial transformations.

matryoshka.a: Matryoshka is a traditional Russian nesting doll, consisting of a set of wooden dolls of decreasing size placed one inside another. Originating in the late 19th century, these dolls are often hand-painted with intricate designs, depicting themes from Russian folklore, family, and nature.
matryoshka.o: Across all four renders, the style combines highly detailed, ornate doll-like figures with sculptural volume, patterned headscarves, and nested or repeated forms. Strong symmetry, close portrait framing, saturated reds and florals, and dramatic dark contrasts give the images a theatrical, unsettling richness.

matt-adnate.a: Matt Adnate is an Australian street artist known for his large-scale murals and portraits that often depict Indigenous Australians and other cultural figures. His work is characterized by a focus on realism and a deep connection to the communities he portrays, often highlighting themes of identity and cultural heritage.
matt-adnate.o: Across all four renders, enormous realistic faces are painted directly onto brick building walls, combining recognizable portraiture with energetic, visible brushwork and scraped or dripping marks. Saturated reds and blues, strong tonal contrast, and graphic linear accents give the murals an expressive, forceful presence while the masonry remains visible through the paint.

matt-bors.a: Matt Bors is an American cartoonist and editor known for his incisive and satirical comic strips. He has contributed to various publications, often focusing on political and social issues with a humorous twist. Bors is recognized for his ability to blend humor with sharp commentary, making his work both entertaining and thought-provoking.
matt-bors.o: The style uses dense comic-book drawing with heavy black contours, flat yet strongly saturated color blocks, and selective crosshatched texture. It repeatedly combines expressive faces, crowded political scenes, animal-headed allegories, urban landmarks, and dramatic fire or protest imagery in a bold, high-contrast graphic-novel treatment.

matt-fraction.a: Matt Fraction is a renowned comic book writer known for his work on series such as "Hawkeye" and "Sex Criminals." His storytelling is characterized by a unique blend of humor, emotion, and innovative narrative techniques, which have earned him critical acclaim and a dedicated fanbase.
matt-fraction.o: Across all four renders, the style uses highly saturated coral, pink, teal, and black with stark tonal separation. Heavy ink contours, dense hatching, flat graphic color fields, and rough splattered textures give the recurring portrait-and-character imagery an intense comic-book presence with surreal visual disruptions.

matt-furie.a: Matt Furie is an American artist and illustrator known for his unique and whimsical style. He gained widespread recognition for creating the character Pepe the Frog, which became an internet meme. Furie's work often features surreal and humorous elements, blending pop culture with fantasy.
matt-furie.o: Across all four paintings, fantastical monster characters are rendered with saturated colors, heavy contour lines, and clearly visible, energetic paint strokes on textured canvas. The expressive faces, exaggerated eyes and mouths, dense imaginative settings, and layered small marks create a playful yet grotesque surreal character-painting style.

matt-groening.a: Matt Groening is an American cartoonist, writer, and producer, best known for creating the iconic television series " The Simpsons " and "Futurama." His work is characterized by its satirical humor, distinctive character designs, and cultural commentary. Groening's influence on animation and pop culture is profound, with " The Simpsons " becoming one of the longest-running TV shows in history.
matt-groening.o: The style combines flat, intensely saturated cartoon color with thick black contours and visible rough brush texture. It consistently exaggerates eyes, mouths, teeth, and anatomy into expressive grotesque characters, while dense crowded compositions alternate with brightly colored storybook environments.

matt-mahurin.a: Matt Mahurin is a renowned American illustrator, photographer, and filmmaker known for his distinctive and evocative visual style. His work often explores themes of social justice, politics, and the human condition, utilizing a blend of surrealism and realism to create thought-provoking imagery. Mahurin's illustrations have appeared in numerous publications, and his artistic influence extends across various media.
matt-mahurin.o: Across all four renders, the style uses a painterly, filmic treatment with heavily muted green-gray colors, deep shadows, and soft atmospheric light. Dense fog obscures distant buildings and figures, while isolated cloaked silhouettes, sparse trees, birds, and recurring red accents create a dark, uncanny fantasy mood.

matt-molloy.a: Matt Molloy is a Canadian photographer known for his innovative technique of time-stacking, where he combines hundreds of photos to create stunning, painterly images of the sky. His work often features dramatic cloud formations and vibrant colors, capturing the passage of time in a single frame.
matt-molloy.o: Across all four landscapes, the sky and reflections are transformed into sweeping, vortex-like bands of visible color, giving the scenes an energetic long-exposure feel. Vivid sunset pinks, oranges, and cool blues combine with luminous horizons, grounded by quiet fields, trees, and water.

matt-rhodes.a: Matt Rhodes is a contemporary illustrator known for his work in the video game industry, particularly as a lead concept artist. His style is characterized by a strong narrative focus, often incorporating elements of fantasy and mythology.
matt-rhodes.o: Across all four images, the style combines densely worked fantasy environments and figures with forceful dark linework, layered textures, and dramatic, expressive compositions. Saturated copper, orange, red, and deep blue-green hues are pushed into strong light-dark contrasts, with glowing suns, fires, and backlit skies creating an epic atmosphere.

matt-sesow.a: Matt Sesow is an American painter known for his raw, emotive, and often chaotic works that explore themes of personal trauma and resilience. His art is characterized by bold colors, distorted figures, and a frenetic energy that challenges traditional notions of beauty and form.
matt-sesow.o: The style combines vivid, high-contrast color blocks with visibly layered, rough paint and energetic black linework. It is densely packed with expressive cartoon-like faces, monster characters, eyes, teeth, symbols, and handwritten marks, creating a surreal, graffiti-like visual field.

matt-wagner.a: Matt Wagner is an American comic book writer and artist known for his work on series like "Grendel" and "Mage." His storytelling often blends elements of fantasy and noir, creating rich, layered narratives that have captivated audiences for decades.
matt-wagner.o: Across all four renders, the style combines visible, energetic brushwork with dense illustrative detail and sharp ink-like contours. It favors dramatic fantasy characters and creatures in high-contrast compositions, shifting between moody forest scenes, stark paper-toned studies, and vivid action-filled tableaux.

matt-wuerker.a: Matt Wuerker is a renowned American political cartoonist and illustrator known for his work with Politico, where he combines sharp wit with detailed and expressive illustrations to comment on contemporary political issues. His style is characterized by a blend of humor and incisive critique, often employing a rich color palette and dynamic compositions.
matt-wuerker.o: Across all four renders, the style combines visibly worked watercolor-like paint with dark, irregular ink contours and highly saturated color. It is densely packed with close-up, caricatured faces whose distorted anatomy, bulging eyes, and exaggerated expressions create a chaotic grotesque-comic mood.

matte-texture.a: Matte texture is a surface finish that lacks gloss and shine, providing a smooth, non-reflective appearance. It is commonly used in various applications, including paint, photography, and digital art, to create a subdued and elegant look.
matte-texture.o: The style presents abstract slabs and fields of pigment as tactile material studies, with visible broad brushwork, built-up impasto, torn edges, and rough relief-like surfaces. It relies on stark dark tones against pale grounds, with one rust-red variation, combining sculptural texture and high-contrast, minimal compositions with generous negative space.

matteo-massagrande.a: Matteo Massagrande is an Italian painter known for his detailed and atmospheric depictions of architectural interiors. His work often explores themes of time, memory, and decay, capturing the beauty of abandoned spaces with a meticulous attention to detail.
matteo-massagrande.o: Across all four renders, the style presents richly observed, abandoned architectural interiors with peeling plaster, aged wood, climbing vegetation, and strong shafts of sunlight. Visible brushwork and textured surfaces combine realistic spatial detail with a subdued, shadow-heavy palette and sharply contrasted illuminated areas.

matthaus-merian-the-elder.a: Matthaus Merian the Elder was a Swiss-born engraver and publisher known for his detailed and precise engravings and etchings during the 17th century. He is celebrated for his topographical works and maps, as well as his contributions to the field of natural history illustration, particularly through his depictions of flora and fauna.
matthaus-merian-the-elder.o: The style combines densely detailed natural-history imagery with fine engraved linework, crosshatching, and hand-colored illustrative forms. Exotic animals, birds, insects, flowers, and tropical plants are arranged as ornamental vignettes against a warm cream ground, producing a vivid yet archival decorative effect.

matthew-barney.a: Matthew Barney is an American contemporary artist known for his innovative and often provocative multimedia works. His art combines performance, sculpture, and film, exploring themes of mythology, identity, and transformation. Barney's most notable work, the "Cremaster Cycle," is a series of five films that blend surreal imagery with complex narratives.
matthew-barney.o: The style presents theatrical, surreal characters and monumental sculptural props in expansive studio or gallery interiors. It relies on densely layered textiles, feathers, scraps, and found materials, with subdued natural light and restrained pink, white, gray, and rust tones creating an elaborate, otherworldly atmosphere.

matthew-pillsbury.a: Matthew Pillsbury is an acclaimed photographer known for his evocative black and white images that explore themes of time and motion. His work often captures the essence of urban life, using long exposure techniques to create ghostly, dreamlike scenes that convey a sense of movement and transience.
matthew-pillsbury.o: The style uses stark black-and-white realism with dramatic architectural interiors, deep shadows, bright shafts of light, and highly detailed surfaces. Long-exposure motion blur turns crowds into translucent, ghostlike forms, creating cinematic, dark, atmospheric scenes with reflective floors and monumental spaces.

matthias-grunewald.a: Matthias Grunewald was a German Renaissance painter known for his expressive and emotionally intense religious works, particularly the Isenheim Altarpiece. His art is characterized by vivid colors, dramatic contrasts, and a deep sense of spirituality and mysticism.
matthias-grunewald.o: The style combines highly detailed, painterly rendering with expressive faces, dense feather and hair textures, and strongly visible fine brushwork. Dark backgrounds, earthy neutrals, muted blues, and saturated red accents create a moody, high-contrast atmosphere across the portraits, figures, and birds.

matthias-haker.a: Matthias Haker is a contemporary photographer known for his captivating images of abandoned and decaying architecture. His work often explores the beauty in forgotten spaces, capturing the intricate details and haunting atmospheres of these environments.
matthias-haker.o: Across all four renders, richly detailed abandoned interiors combine decayed architecture with dense ornamental plasterwork, carved wood, stained glass, and elaborate ceilings. Strong shafts of sunlight cut through shadowed spaces, producing vivid teal, amber, and rust tones, while exaggerated perspective and monumental ruins create a dark, epic, slightly surreal atmosphere.

matthias-heiderich.a: Matthias Heiderich is a contemporary German photographer known for his striking architectural and urban photography. His work often features vibrant colors, geometric compositions, and a minimalist aesthetic, capturing the beauty and simplicity of urban environments.
matthias-heiderich.o: These architectural street scenes use realistic, highly detailed photography with strong geometric forms, repeated structures, and sculptural concrete surfaces. Saturated turquoise, coral, cream, and red colors are sharpened by bright directional sunlight and deep shadows, giving the images a bold retro-modern character.

matthias-jung.a: Matthias Jung is a contemporary German artist known for his surreal and imaginative photomontages, often blending architectural elements with dreamlike landscapes. His work explores the boundaries of reality and fantasy, creating whimsical and thought-provoking compositions.
matthias-jung.o: The style presents highly realistic, carefully detailed architectural scenes with solitary, decaying towers set against expansive rural landscapes. Subdued natural colors, clear cinematic light, and strange gravity-defying or otherwise impossible buildings create a dreamy, surreal atmosphere while preserving convincing material texture and architectural weight.

mattias-adolfsson.a: Mattias Adolfsson is a Swedish illustrator known for his intricate and whimsical drawings that often depict fantastical worlds and imaginative scenes. His work is characterized by detailed line work and a playful, humorous style that captures the viewer's imagination.
mattias-adolfsson.o: Across all four renders, the style builds densely populated fantasy environments from fine black linework, clean illustrative shapes, and many tiny architectural and character details. Restrained cream grounds contrast with saturated red, orange, teal, and muted blue accents, while oversized creatures, impossible structures, and crowded vignettes create a whimsical surreal atmosphere.

maud-humphrey.a: Maud Humphrey is an American illustrator known for her charming and detailed illustrations, particularly of children and women in Victorian and Edwardian settings. She was active during the late 19th and early 20th centuries and was the mother of actor Humphrey Bogart. Her work often features romantic and nostalgic themes, capturing the innocence and elegance of her subjects.
maud-humphrey.o: This style presents idealized female portraits with softly modeled faces, flowing curled hair, elaborate floral adornments, and delicate period clothing. Warm cream grounds, pastel pinks and greens, visible brushwork, and ornate oval or circular frames create a refined decorative portrait aesthetic.

maud-lewis.a: Maud Lewis was a Canadian folk artist known for her brightly colored and charming depictions of rural life in Nova Scotia. Despite facing significant physical challenges and financial hardships, she created a joyful and whimsical body of work that has become beloved in Canadian art history. Her paintings often feature simple, yet vibrant scenes of nature, animals, and rural settings, capturing the essence of her surroundings with a unique and naive artistic style.
maud-lewis.o: Across all four renders, the style uses saturated, cheerful colors and dense flower-filled scenes populated by simplified animals, cottages, trees, and seasonal details.
